docs.x: On the third incident, the county's lord is told. Something Stalks gives him five answers: look into it himself, put his spymaster on it, post a bounty, send for a hunter, or write it off as superstition and keep bleeding control. Looking into it is an intrigue duel against how well the creature hides, which scales with its power. Winning reveals the culprit to him by name. The spymaster runs the same duel with a bonus for being a schemer, and a Trailsman turns the compelled-county version into a far better one. Post a bounty creates a real task contract that any landless adventurer hunter can take off the board: the county's menace, with a purse on it. That needs the landless expansion. Send for a hunter needs nothing. Three letters go out with names on them, and the lord is shown three men in the order of what they are asking for. The roster is built nearest first: the man in your own hall, then the men who owe you, then the world. The fee starts at 60 and rates on the hunter's own reputation rather than the lord's purse: you are paying for the man, not haggling from your ledger. The hunter can accept, refuse, or write back naming a higher price, which doubles it. A county can only be answered once, because the first lord to write stamps it for ten years, so two lords can never both have a man on the same trail. And a hunter who holds both a bounty contract and a summons for the same county is paid twice, which is deliberate.

docs.x: A hunter is the only playable role in the mod that is not a monster, and the game will not let you be both. Vampire, werewolf, hybrid, demon, witch, necromancer and warlock are all written into the Hunter trait as opposites, so the engine refuses the pair outright. The trait gives +3 diplomacy, +2 learning, +4 prowess, +2 advantage and +5 life expectancy, and it has two tracks rather than one. They are not variations on a theme: Track What filling it makes you Monster-Hunter A fighter. Across the full track: +12 prowess, +10 diplomacy, +5 advantage, a quarter more knight effectiveness and cheaper holy orders. It is what the hunt itself reads at almost every point. Witch-Hunter A schemer. +14 on hostile scheme success, +10 baseline dread , +8 life expectancy, doubled diplomatic range, better piety, and four supply-cancelling terrain traits. It is what exorcism and the witch hunt read. There is no inheritance and no random roll on the trait itself: a hunter is always made. Four doors: the ruler designer, the background distribution roll at game start, training, and a handful of story events. Two of those story events are how word of a witch or a monster reaches a court. Witch Spotted opens in a market, and only for a ruler whose faith does not accept witchcraft; Monster Sighting opens in a tavern. Burn the witch at the end of the first, or kill the creature at the end of the second, and a character who was not a hunter becomes one. A hunter gets one or the other in up to one year in five. Everyone else gets them in fewer than one year in fifty. That split came in 2.35a: 2.35 briefly gave the whole map the hunters' rate, and the world filled with new hunters and werewolves. Training one Two interactions, and neither costs a coin. Train Character as a Hunter is the offer; Ask Character to Train You is the mirror, and it is player-only. The AI never asks, and to use it you must already know the other person is a hunter. The gates are worth knowing: the trainee must be at least 13 , must not already be partway through someone else's training, and must not have turned you down in the last five years. All three are recent. It used to be possible to train a four-year-old, and pressing the button twice used to queue two copies of the whole chain onto the same person. Training takes a specialisation early, monsters or witches, and then runs about three months before the night that decides whether it took. An AI hunter only ever offers this to someone who already likes them. An apprentice whose training did not finish can be brought on a hunt instead. If that hunt finds its creature or drives it off, they graduate at the door with a head start on the track. If it ends in a withdrawal they do not: there was no lesson in it. The lifestyle Two focuses, Monster Hunter and Witch-Hunter, worth +3 martial and +3 intrigue respectively, and those attribute points are the whole mechanical payload of a focus here. Everything else in a focus is the AI deciding what kind of hunter it wants to be. Two trees of eight perks each. The Monster Hunter tree has two roots that converge on The Witcher , which grants the True Monster Hunter trait: +5 prowess, +3 martial, half a prestige a month, and +35 life expectancy . Stacked with Built Different's +10 and the trait's own +5, a finished monster hunter lives fifty years longer than he would have. The Witch-Hunter tree ends at True Witch Hunter , and several of its perks actually unlock things rather than just adding numbers: Anti-Mage , the root, opens witch trials and the old witch-hunting decision. Combat Spells reaches the Witcher's elixirs, letting a hunter brew potions without being a witch. Protection Runes grants the witch tree's own protective perk, which more than thirty magic gates read. It did nothing

docs.x: The hunter's regiment. Skirmishers, 50 to a stack and ten sub-regiments at the cap, needing both the Hunter trait and the Hunter Academy perk to raise or reinforce, so an heir can field an inherited regiment but cannot replace its losses until he has earned the perk himself. They do not out-fight monsters and are not meant to. One vampire sub-regiment hits for 1,850 and takes 1,750; a full trainee stack hits for 700 and takes 900. The counter is the point: a quarter against monsters and animals, and a tenth against demonic knights. A maxed hunter's guard neutralises one monster regiment, not an army of them. Fielding them is also one of the ways the county lends you its men at the door.

docs.x: Hunters have secrets too. Depending on what your faith and your liege's faith think of hunters, you either carry a hidden Hunter secret or the open Known Hunter trait, which is +15 from other hunters and −20 from everything else, and gives creature-friendly faiths a crime to charge you with. Faiths take the same four positions on hunters as they do on every other kind: criminal, shunned, accepted, or virtuous.

docs.x: Six lifestyles, ten trees, and they are not priced the same. What a lifestyle costs per level, and how many trees it has to spend those levels on, is most of what separates the creatures in a long game. Lifestyle Per level Base gain Trees Ends at Vampire 1,500 30 Vampirism, 10 perks True Vampire Werewolf 1,100 27 Lycanthropy, 8 perks True Werewolf Hunter 1,400 25 Monster Hunter and Witch-Hunter, 8 each The Witcher / True Witch Hunter Hybrid 1,500 30 Vampire and Werewolf, 9 each Both capstones, then the master focus Magic 1,000 25 Witchcraft 8, Arcane 7, Black Magic 6 True Witch / Mage / Warlock Demon 1,000 25 Demon, 17 perks Greater Demon and Crossroad Dealmaker The werewolf is the cheapest creature to advance and has the least to buy. The hybrid pays the most per level and has eighteen perks to get through, which is why its own code puts the full cost at around 27,000 lifestyle experience on top of two full trait tracks. The demon's tree is the largest single tree in the mod and is designed to be finished and then abandoned: taking both capstones closes the lifestyle behind you. Every creature lifestyle also has a master focus that unlocks only when you hold the capstone. It grants a broad spread of attributes and, deliberately, no further lifestyle experience at all . The road is finished; what is left is power. Two problems in this area were fixed and are worth knowing about because they change how the AI behaves. Before 2.32 only the root perk of each tree carried a weight, so an AI entered a tree and stopped; every perk now carries one and the AI climbs. And a hunter holding a magic artefact used to be outbid into a magic focus, because the hunter focuses sat at a flat weight while the magic ones stacked past it. The creature focuses now all multiply themselves down for a hunter rather than zeroing, so a hunter can end up there, it simply stops being his first pick.

docs.x: There are 22 rules across 85 settings , in two tabs: eleven under Supernatural and eleven under Witchcraft . None of the Supernatural settings blocks achievements; seven Witchcraft ones do. These are the ones that change your game the most: Rule Default Why you might change it Embrace Decisions Off Turn it on and you get the eight decisions that let you become, or stop being, a vampire, werewolf, hybrid or hunter at will. With it off there is no cure for anything. Trait Distribution Counts and below Decides who in the world can be born supernatural. On puts it on everyone; Off gives you a world with no creatures in it but the eight Mikaelsons. Confer Death On Seven settings from Off through NPC-only to More Death. It governs the vampire embrace and the hybrid turning, and, as a trap, not the werewolf wound. AI Confer On Whether AI creatures turn and train other people, and which kinds are allowed to. Set it to Off for a world where you are the only one spreading anything. Inheritance / Pregnancy Werewolf trait only Eight settings covering who can have children with whom and what comes out. One setting is labelled Skip this Setting and means it. Demon Inheritance On Separate from the above. Off is the original behaviour, where demon pregnancies were always lost. Events On Four settings. You can have embrace events only, everything except embrace events, or none. Paleness Vampires Whether turning lightens your skin, and whether that applies to hybrids too. Ageing Stops at portrait maturity How an immortal's portrait behaves over centuries. Visual Changes Off Turns on five cosmetic right-click options. Off by default, so most players never see them. Reset Lifetime Events Every 50 years Lets once-per-lifetime event chains come round again for immortals, who otherwise exhaust them. The Witchcraft tab covers whether you can be a witch at all, how many mages the world generates, how witch hunters behave, the range of spells, arena mode, demonic aggression, Bael, and the endgame crises. The Supernatural settings take their text from one file; the Witchcraft settings take theirs from seven different files scattered among event text. If a Witchcraft rule's description ever reads oddly, that is why.

docs.x: Fifty-five decisions across three files, and more than a hundred character interactions. Almost none of it costs money. The currency in this mod is cooldowns, risk and exposure. The Supernatural eleven Eight of them are the embrace and abandon pair for each of vampire, werewolf, hybrid and hunter, and all eight are behind the Embrace Decisions rule, which ships off. The AI can never take any of them. The other three are the feeding decisions, and they are what 2.35 rebuilt: Decision Who Your cooldown What it does Satiate Thirst Vampire 7 years Three days later, the feeding chain Satiate Hunger Werewolf 5 years Three days later, the hunt chain Satiate Hunger/Thirst Hybrid 7 years A coin flip between the two None of them costs anything. An AI creature runs on its own fourteen-year cadence rather than your cooldown. These were broken in instructive ways. The vampire decision was entirely commented out before 2.32, so pure vampires had no feeding decision at all, and the familiar coin-flip belonged to the hybrid. All three then had their AI check interval set to zero, which means the AI never looks at a decision: twelve years of a fresh campaign with about ninety-six vampires in it produced zero feeds and zero trails . Interactions The Supernatural layer's own interactions are the eleven turning interactions (offer, force and ask for each kind, plus the two hunter training ones), the two vampire social interactions, Compulsion and Ask for Blood, the werewolf and hybrid Shapeshift, and five cosmetic right-click options that are hidden unless you turn the Visual Changes rule on. The Witchcraft layer adds fifty-four more, which are the spells. One file is worth mentioning because it is not there: a cross-species duel interaction, a challenge between vampires, werewolves, hybrids and hunters, fully written with AI weighting and species-awareness. It ships as 462 lines of comment and nothing else. It has no localisation and nothing references it. It is the largest piece of dead content in the mod.

docs.x: Ten men-at-arms regiments: five from the Supernatural layer, five from Witchcraft. They are priced in four different currencies, and two of them are free to keep. Regiment Who can raise it Cost Damage / toughness Stack Wolves Any werewolf or hybrid 65 prestige 100 / 75 10 Werewolves Lycanthropy 50 100 prestige 215 / 185 5 Bats Any vampire or hybrid Gold 5 / 5 250 Vampires Vampirism 50 100 piety 185 / 175 10 Hunter Trainees Hunter + Hunter Academy 60 gold 14 / 18 50, ten sub-regiments Cultists A coven culture, or a camp that unlocks them 50 gold 15 / 14 100 Skeleton Warriors A necromancer 200 prestige 20 / 14 100 Demonic Knights The demon tree's Infernal Guardians 1,000 prestige 300 / 80 100 Battle Golems A finished golem project 1,000 gold 250 / 100 100 Baba Yaga's hut Yaga, with the house 1,000 gold 1,000 / 100 10, exactly one ever Vampires are the only thing in the game maintained in piety as well as gold ; wolves and werewolves are maintained in prestige. Skeletons cost nothing to keep at either maintenance level, so a necromancer fields a thousand free skeletons for prestige alone. The creature regiments cannot be borrowed through a vassal, because every one of them refuses to be raised through a subject. Two counters in the files do not work , and the files say so. Bats claim a bonus against werewolves and werewolves claim one against vampires, but a counter key has to name a regiment type , and both of those are keys whose type is Monster. They are inert. Hunter Trainees' counters are written correctly and do work. Artifacts Every artefact in the mod is created at runtime by an event or an effect. There is no artefact type declared anywhere, and no fixed list to collect: there is one template , marked unique and impossible to reforge, and sixteen visual keys hung off it. What you can end up carrying includes the Darkblade, the Crown of Shadows, a black grimoire, dragonscales, rings of life, death and power, two ancient singularities, a witch's amulet, Baba Yaga's broom, a magic orb, Hell's Scepter, a witch hunter's crossbow, Merlin's wand, and the eleven potions. Only the Darkblade and Merlin's wand have real per-culture art; the rest borrow a vanilla mesh.

docs.x: Supernatural runs on the base game and needs nothing else. The compatibility questions that matter come from what it replaces, and from one specific pair of mods you must not run beside it. Do not run this alongside Witchcraft or V&L. Supernatural already carries that content. Loading either next to it puts two copies of the same files against each other, and whichever loads second wins outright. Also known not to get along: AGOT: Battlefield Duels , Better Barbershop , Asia Expansion Project and Cultural Armies Pack . Load order with AGOT A Game of Thrones AGOT submods AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai (optional) Supernatural AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch — always last The patch is a separate subscription and it exists because both mods define the same twenty-two entries: marriages, secrets, disinheritance, the witch ritual, birth events, schemes, abductions and more. The patch merges them so neither mod silently erases the other's work. One of those entries, the marriage-acceptance rule, was behind multiplayer desyncs in testing. What it replaces CK3 resolves mod files by path, last loaded wins. A mod file sitting at the same path as a base-game file replaces that file entirely . Anything the vanilla copy defined and the replacement does not is simply gone. Most of Supernatural is new filenames, which collide with nothing. The exceptions are the places it deliberately steps on vanilla: the birth on-actions, the death on-actions, several character interactions including disinheritance, some scripted relations, travel options, a handful of secret effects, and a set of portrait and accessory gene files. The mod ships its own list of these. Two mods that both replace the same vanilla file are mutually exclusive in practice. That, rather than anything specific to witches, is why Witchcraft and V&L cannot sit beside this one. Mid-save Adding it to a running campaign mostly works, and it is built for it in places: existing saves get a one-time repair pass for secrets nobody was told about, creatures that predate the disease-immunity flag are retro-fitted on a yearly pulse, characters stuck mid-transition are released, and the hunt's availability check is written to fail open on a continued save rather than grey the activity out forever. Two things do not carry over. Game rules are chosen when a save is created , so a campaign started without Supernatural has no values for its twenty-two rules. And the mod adds portrait and accessory genes, which is the usual CK3 hazard around adding or removing a mod mid-save. Removing it from a save is not supported and there is no uninstall path. Most of what strands is mod-created and disappears with the mod. The exception worth knowing: the mod writes three doctrines onto every pagan faith in the save at game start, and those are vanilla faith objects that persist. Nothing takes them off again. Multiplayer Every player needs the same mods at the same positions. The mod honours CK3's own multiplayer murder-scheme protections in its own scheme, and carries no other multiplayer-specific code. The game version it is built against is 1.19.0.6 .

docs.x: Eight language folders ship, and only one of them is maintained. Language State English Complete and maintained. 56 files. Spanish Real translation, contributed by Luke0704, and behind the current English text. Russian Real translation, and behind the current English text. French, German, Korean, Polish English text under a translated header. All four are byte-for-byte identical to each other on every file. Simplified Chinese The same English text again, and every file is exactly six bytes larger than the French one, which is the length of its header line. Nothing is broken by this; a player in one of those five languages simply sees English rather than missing keys. The Workshop page does not claim any language support, so it is not a broken promise. But if you play in French, German, Korean, Polish or Chinese, expect English.

docs.x: The mod shows its own changelog once per save, at game start or on the next 1 January after an update. This is what it says, condensed. 2.35a — The witch you let live Fixes for The Hunt, safe on a running save. Turning down a witch hunt no longer kills the witch, so witches married into other courts stop vanishing. The witch and monster sightings are fast for hunters only and back to their old rate for everyone else, which stops the world filling with new hunters and werewolves. Monster Sighting now has the same conditions as its twin, so it no longer reaches someone imprisoned, incapable, travelling or busy with an activity. An ordinary murder no longer reads as a creature's kill unless the killer was there; a murder in your own hall still can. Characters already in House Hellion stay there. 2.35 — The Hunt A new activity: ride out and hunt what is killing people. Kills and prowling leave trails on the counties they happen in, and trails escalate: three incidents and the lord hears about it. He can look into it himself, set his spymaster on it, post a bounty, or send for a named hunter and pay him when it is done. A new court position, the Trailsman, reads the countryside. You can hunt a creature or hunt a witch, each with their own trails and beats. Bring silver, stakes, dogs or men, and the door goes differently. Take an apprentice along and he graduates in the field. The creature gets the other half of the scene, and real answers: stand and fight, go to ground, compel him, send your progeny, let the wolf out, or talk him onto somebody worse. Get away and you can warn your sire and your get, or sell them. Demons argue instead of running, and may offer a bargain. Hunters and creatures earn names the world starts using. A county that turns three hunters away stops attracting any. You can cover your own kills: pay it off, frame someone, or hide the body. Compel a whole town and the holes start to line up. Hunters ride at bad odds far less often, and can turn back. Fixes: witch hunts were impossible to reach and now work; two files never loaded, so no trail was ever written; the hunter migration layer never ran; hunters are told about witches and monsters far more often; secret witches leave trails, not only openly known ones; compelling someone for their secrets no longer errors; thousands of script errors a session removed; hunter regiments now need the Hunter Academies perk. Earlier Version What it was 2.34a Your spymaster stops finding secrets you already know; makers, sires, trainers and parents know what they made; existing saves repaired once on load. 2.34 — the blood remembers who Turnings are remembered and name your maker. Six one-off events grow out of those memories. A maxed vampire can compel a hunter to go home. True Witch Hunter and True Monster Hunter capstones. Vampires can feed on tribal holdings. 2.33 — the blood remembers Fall in battle with vampire blood in you and rise. Weeks of hunger, then feed or refuse for good. Whoever gave you the blood becomes your maker. Works landed or landless, and needs no patch. 2.32 Feed in foreign cities. Vampires get their Satiate Thirst decision back. Two new vampire branches and two new werewolf branches. Surviving a hunter makes you stronger. Werewolves are named by tier, like vampires. 2.31c Dragons, wights, Others and the Night King can no longer be turned, compelled or cursed. 130 spell tooltips showed a raw key. The eight Originals use AGOT's current portrait genes. 2.31a A werewolf bite festers one to three years first. A quarter of NPC werewolves were spawning as vampires. Demon-blooded children grow into demons in their twenties.

docs.t: Download The Long Night & Azor Ahai — CK3 mod without Steam
docs.x: Manual install Download without Steam The mod is plain files, so it runs on any copy of Crusader Kings III: GOG, Epic, Game Pass, wherever you bought it. It takes about five minutes by hand, and this page walks the whole thing. Home › Mods › The Long Night › Download If your CK3 is on Steam, use the Workshop instead It's one click, it updates itself the moment I push a fix, and it handles the load order for you. Nothing on this page is better; it exists for people who can't use the Workshop at all. Subscribe on the Steam Workshop → Step zero Get the files The mod is open source. The repository is the download, with no mirror, no shortener and no waiting. Download from GitHub Browse the source current release on GitHub CK3 1.19.0.6 requires A Game of Thrones mid-save safe On the newest release, take the file named AGOT-The-Long-Night-and-Azor-Ahai- version .zip under Assets (the version number matches the release). It is about 25 MB and holds exactly the mod and nothing else. The two Source code entries below it are the whole repository, which is a much larger download you don't need. Five minutes Installing it by hand Unzip it The archive unpacks straight to a single folder, the-long-night-azor-ahai , containing common , events , gfx , localization and a descriptor.mod . There's no outer wrapper folder to dig through. That folder is the whole mod. A few workshop_changelog text files sit inside it as well. They are notes from past updates; the game ignores them, so leave them be. What the archive does not include is the second file the launcher needs: a the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod that sits beside the folder rather than inside it. You'll make that in step 3, and it's a copy-paste. Move both into your CK3 mod directory The folder and the .mod file go here together, and the .mod file sits next to the folder, never inside it: Windows Documents\Paradox Interactive\Crusader Kings III\mod\ macOS ~/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ Linux ~/.local/share/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/ If there's no mod folder there yet, launch CK3 once and close it, or create the folder yourself. Make the .mod file (don't skip this one) This is the step that decides whether any of the rest works, and it is not optional . The launcher does not read the descriptor.mod inside the mod folder. It reads a separate the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod file sitting in the mod directory next to the folder, and that one isn't in the archive, because it has to describe where the mod lives on your machine. So make it. In your mod folder, create a new plain text file named the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod , open it in any editor (Notepad is fine) and paste this in: copy version="1.1.3" picture="thumbnail.png" tags={ "Events" "Warfare" "Historical" "Religion" "Culture" "Gameplay" } name="AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai" supported_version="1.19.0.6" path="mod/the-long-night-azor-ahai" Two details matter here. path= is relative : it says "the the-long-night-azor-ahai folder inside mod ", which is true on every machine, so use it exactly as written rather than typing a full C:\ path. And the remote_file_id line is left out by design: that line tells the launcher "this is a Steam Workshop item", which is exactly what your copy isn't, and leaving it in is a good way to have the launcher ignore your folder or replace it. If you took a Source code archive instead of the built one, it does contain a the-long-night-azor-ahai.mod , but it's the copy from my machine, with my folder path baked into it. Overwrite its contents with the block above and it'll behave. Make sure your text editor saves it as .mod and not .mod.txt . On Windows you may need to turn on file extensions to see the difference. Enable it and set the load order Open the Paradox launcher, go to All installed mods , and the mod should be listed. Add it to a playset, then order it like this: A Game of Thrones (required, and it also needs a manual install if you're not on Steam) AGOT submods: AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility… AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Optional: Supernatural If you run Supernatural: the Compatibility Patch, always last Before you start a game The one rule Disable every other Long Night mod AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked in your playset . Sorting them below this one is not enough; they have to be disabled . This mod is a fork of both and ships files at the same paths, so either one loaded anywhere overrides it with older code and brings back the see-through dragon bug. If you installed those manually too, the surest fix is to delete their folders and their .mod files outright. When it goes wrong Troubleshooting "Descriptor file error" The path= line is wrong. It's the cause almost every time. Use forward slashes , never backslashes, even on Windows. The path must match your folder name exactly, including case. If the relative path won't take, use the full one instead: path="C:/Users/YourName/Documents/Paradox Interactive/Crusader Kings III/mod/the-long-night-azor-ahai" It doesn't appear at all Check the file is .mod , not .mod.txt . Check it's in the mod folder itself, not inside the mod's own folder. Check you removed the remote_file_id line. With it left in, the launcher may look for a Workshop copy instead of yours. Restart the launcher fully; it scans on start. Confirm the folder itself contains common and events , not another folder that contains them. If you're still stuck, the Long Night Discord is the fastest place to get it sorted; manual-install questions get answered there daily. Common questions Manual install FAQ Do I still need A Game of Thrones? Yes, always. This is a submod: it adds the Long Night endgame to AGOT rather than replacing it. If you're not on Steam you'll need to install AGOT manually as well, the same way, and load it above this mod. Will it update itself? No. A manual install is a snapshot of one version. When I push an update you'll want to delete the old mod folder, unzip the new one in its place, and change the version= line in your .mod file to match. Watching the repository or joining the Discord is the easiest way to know when that happens. Is this the same build as the Workshop version? It's the same source the Workshop build is cut from, and the repository is where updates land first. The one thing worth doing is checking the version number in the Paradox launcher against the version on the Workshop page . That matters in multiplayer, where everyone has to be on the same version or the game refuses to start. Which file do I take on the releases page? The one named AGOT-The-Long-Night-and-Azor-Ahai- followed by the version number. That's the built archive, around 25 MB and only the mod. The two Source code entries underneath are the entire repository including development files; they work, but they're a far bigger download for the same mod. Can I use it with an existing save? Yes, it's mid-save safe to add and to update. The one caveat is that CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. Where's the source? The repository is public , so you can read every file, open an issue, or fork it. It's built on the work of others and it seemed only right to pass that along the same way. Does the mod work on Mac and Linux? It's script and assets rather than compiled code, so yes. Only the folder location differs, and both paths are in step 2. Standing on other people's work. This mod is a fork built on Freeholder 's original Long Night, Tehaen 's 1.19 update, and Wepo94 's The Long Night+, and on the AGOT team's total conversion underneath all of it. If you enjoy this, that's where it started. While you're here What the mod does If you landed here for the download and haven't seen it, the full breakdown is worth a look : the wights with their own realms, the playable Night's Watch, the Azor Ahai prophecy, and a riddle at the bottom for anyone who reads to the end. If you run Supernatural as well, it has its own manual install guide now, and the compatibility patch still goes last.

docs.t: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai — a CK3 Game of Thrones mod
docs.x: A CK3 mod for A Game of Thrones The Long Night & Azor Ahai "There is only one war that matters. The Great War. And it is here." Eight seasons promised us the Long Night. We got one dark episode and a knife. The best version of that story is still unwritten, and a game where you play a lord in Westeros is a very good place to write it. Subscribe on Steam Workshop Read the wiki Download without Steam Join the Discord Version 1.1.3 Requires A Game of Thrones CK3 1.19.0.6 English, Russian, Spanish & French Mid-save safe Home › Mods › The Long Night & Azor Ahai 13,600+ current subscribers 26,000+ unique visitors 700+ favorites 4 phases, across a century 31,000+ views on the showcase The showcase Watch it play out first The whole mod in one video: the invasion, the Watch, the prophecy, and what the map looks like when it's over. The Long Night & Azor Ahai — Full CK3 AGOT Mod Showcase. Plays here, or watch it on YouTube . The mod in full What this is, start to finish The Long Night & Azor Ahai is a submod for A Game of Thrones , the Crusader Kings III total conversion, and it does one thing: it builds the Long Night out into the endgame the setting always pointed at. It is free, it lives on the Steam Workshop, and it has shipped thirty-one updates since 8 August 2026, most of them built from what players reported in the Discord and the comments. The current version is 1.1.1. The invasion is a struggle in four phases that you can watch coming for decades. When it arrives, the Night King is a character with a court, a culture, a faith and a realm of his own, and every lord he beats gets back up wearing his own face, keeping his own title and answering to a new liege. Dragons that die over his ground come back on his side. The Wall comes down at Castle Black with the camera on it. His host grows with what he takes: twenty thousand beyond the Wall, fifty once the far north is his, a hundred thousand when the Wall falls, two hundred thousand when the North does, scaled by the difficulty you chose and capped at half a million, the population of King's Landing. The living have a lot to do about it. You can take the black and mean it: lay down your lands, hand the realm to your heir, and hold one of the Wall's castles or ride with one of eight ranging companies as a landless captain. As Lord Commander you can call a Great Ranging and pay two hundred brothers for the answer, or send a sworn brother down the length of Westeros asking every lord how full his dungeons are. Southern lords can send men and grain north, empty their cells onto the Wall in one order, mine dragonglass, bring a red priest into the hall, and ask him for the one blessing a priest can give once in his life. Since 1.1.0 the fight with the Night King is no longer a dice roll. Reaching him opens the Last Hour, a Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and the people who were there with you against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Castle steel does not bite. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own way through the fight, and kin can take the blow meant for you. Only a bane destroys him; ordinary steel casts him down and the dark crowns another. Lose, and he keeps you: your character is raised as one of his, and a later champion may find you standing on the wrong side of the line. Underneath all of it runs the prophecy. Every character in the world is measured against nine marks, continuously, and the AI competes for the naming as hard as you do. Red priests, witches and greenseers say the name out loud; Lightbringer can be forged at the price every version of the tale agrees on; and whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain and revealed once, at the end. Then comes the Dawn: a scoured North, the Question of the North, colonists and free folk filling the empty land, and a record of the men who were standing there when it ended. This page is the overview. The wiki is the complete reference, every mechanic with the numbers on one page; the Workshop page is the short version, and the GitHub wiki carries the full version history. Read this part Before you play: one rule Disable every other Long Night mod AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked in your playset . Sorting them below this one is not enough; they have to be disabled . This mod grew out of both and ships files at the same paths. Either of them loaded anywhere in your list overrides this mod with older code and brings back the see-through dragon bug. This mod replaces both, so you can unsubscribe from them entirely. What you'll play The dead get back up This is an invasion with characters, politics and a body count you recognise, and the lords you lose come back as the enemy. A risen lord, with the same face, the same title and a new liege. An Other, ruling as a character in his own right. The Night King himself, with 288K men behind him. Wights are characters, not troops Every man you lose can rise wearing his own face. Wights keep their own portraits, their own titles and their own rot, and rule their own realms under the Night King. They raise what they kill Bring a dragon down over the Haunted Forest and it comes back with the same name and the same face, the wrong colour and the wrong rider. The Wall comes down on camera The collapse at Castle Black is a scripted scene rather than a pop-up notification, and thirty days later a card opens in your own station, whether you were a sworn brother on the Wall that morning, a free folk chief, a dragonrider, a northman, a red priest, a lord, or nobody at all. Take the black, and mean it Lay down your lands, hand the realm to your heir, and serve. Hold one of the Wall's nineteen castles as a sworn brother, or ride out with one of eight ranging companies, landless and oathbound, each with a real camp on the map from day one. Captains compete for First Ranger. Decisions only the Lord Commander gets Call a Great Ranging north for word, and pay two hundred brothers for it. Or send a sworn brother gate to gate down the length of Westeros, asking every great lord the old question: how full are your dungeons, and what were you planning to do with the men inside them? Southern lords have a stake Send Men and Grain to the Watch: a cart, a season's stores, or your whole vault. The Watch keeps a list, and it decides what they'll do for you later. Or send the dungeons to the Wall in one order: every prisoner who can take the black, and a reason for each one who cannot. How it ends The Night King is fought on foot Added in 1.1.0. Beating the dead in the field once opens the War for the Dawn; reaching him opens this. The Last Hour A Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and your companions against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Prowess counts for half against them, so a great swordsman with castle steel loses eventually. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own option and change the fight. Kin and friends on your line can take the blow meant for you. The numbers are in the wiki. Only a bane destroys him Dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire. Ordinary steel only casts him down: within days he rises again, the same face and the same name, and the Long Night goes on. Whoever lands the killing blow is Azor Ahai Reborn, marks or no marks, named or not. Lose, and he keeps you Your character is raised as one of his before the card even opens, tells you what it felt like, and is his from then on. You play on as your heir. A later champion may find you standing on his side of the line. The spear If the dead field no dragon of their own, he can bring one down in battle. Every rider present is a target; the odds run from about forty percent against a hatchling to five against something Balerion's size, and they climb beyond the Wall. The rider rolls to live. The dragon is taken, not killed, and comes back under him with its own name and history. The Wall is a ward A rider can force a dragon across a standing Wall anyway (the AI is likelier to try it the less it knows), and a Night King met beyond an intact Wall is near-certain to take that dragon. Once the Wall is breached, the ward is gone and dragons fly where they like. White Walkers before the Long Night During Winter Is Coming, rangers and northern lords can meet a lone Walker before the dead have taken a single county: a small melee, one Walker against a handful of men, with the Sam Tarly outcome in the deck. Died, and came back A red priest can spend himself on one person, once, ever. A blessed man who falls in battle gets the argument: a card when you go down, the priest's decision two days later, and a Get up button to press when he pays. Each return needs a fresh priest and takes more out of you. How to set it up, step by step. The record The character page remembers it: the Walker you killed, the night you faced him and lived, the steel that broke in your hand, the day the Wall fell, who paid to bring you ba

As Lord Commander you can call a Great Ranging and pay two hundred brothers for the answer, or send a sworn brother down the length of Westeros asking every lord how full his dungeons are. Southern lords can send men and grain north, empty their cells onto the Wall in one order, mine dragonglass, bring a red priest into the hall, and ask him for the one blessing a priest can give once in his life. Since 1.1.0 the fight with the Night King is no longer a dice roll. Reaching him opens the Last Hour, a Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and the people who were there with you against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Castle steel does not bite. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own way through the fight, and kin can take the blow meant for you. Only a bane destroys him; ordinary steel casts him down and the dark crowns another. Lose, and he keeps you: your character is raised as one of his, and a later champion may find you standing on the wrong side of the line. Underneath all of it runs the prophecy. Every character in the world is measured against nine marks, continuously, and the AI competes for the naming as hard as you do. Red priests, witches and greenseers say the name out loud; Lightbringer can be forged at the price every version of the tale agrees on; and whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain and revealed once, at the end. Then comes the Dawn: a scoured North, the Question of the North, colonists and free folk filling the empty land, and a record of the men who were standing there when it ended. This page is the overview. The wiki is the complete reference, every mechanic with the numbers on one page; the Workshop page is the short version, and the GitHub wiki carries the full version history.

The Last Hour A Trial-of-Seven melee in the snow: you and your companions against him and his White Walkers, blow by blow. Prowess counts for half against them, so a great swordsman with castle steel loses eventually. Lightbringer, Valyrian steel and dragonglass each open their own option and change the fight. Kin and friends on your line can take the blow meant for you. The numbers are in the wiki. Only a bane destroys him Dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire. Whoever lands the killing blow is Azor Ahai Reborn, marks or no marks, named or not. Lose, and he keeps you Your character is raised as one of his before the card even opens, tells you what it felt like, and is his from then on. You play on as your heir. A later champion may find you standing on his side of the line. The spear If the dead field no dragon of their own, he can bring one down in battle. Every rider present is a target; the odds run from about forty percent against a hatchling to five against something Balerion's size, and they climb beyond the Wall. The rider rolls to live. The dragon is taken, not killed, and comes back under him with its own name and history. The Wall is a ward A rider can force a dragon across a standing Wall anyway (the AI is likelier to try it the less it knows), and a Night King met beyond an intact Wall is near-certain to take that dragon. White Walkers before the Long Night During Winter Is Coming, rangers and northern lords can meet a lone Walker before the dead have taken a single county: a small melee, one Walker against a handful of men, with the Sam Tarly outcome in the deck. Died, and came back A red priest can spend himself on one person, once, ever. A blessed man who falls in battle gets the argument: a card when you go down, the priest's decision two days later, and a Get up button to press when he pays. Each return needs a fresh priest and takes more out of you. How to set it up, step by step. docs.x: The struggle Each phase changes what your counties produce and how close the dead are. Dead dragons, lost rangings and a hollowed-out Watch all move the tracker, so you can plan your preparations against something you can see. THE LONG SUMMER Peace, a +5% county modifier , and a counter you can see from day one. This is the window you get to spend. WINTER IS COMING −5% county modifier. Length is unknown, and your own losses shorten it. THE LONG NIGHT The invasion, at a −10% county modifier . Dragonglass in the cellars and men sent north is the whole difference between surviving it and being surprised by it. THE DAWN A ruined North to rebuild, and one crown-level choice that outlasts the war. The same tracker in the Long Summer, Winter Is Coming and the Long Night. The catalyst list underneath is what moved it. A quiet century still ends on schedule. A bad one ends early.

docs.s: Azor Ahai has a whole system behind it
docs.x: The prophecy There is no Azor Ahai trait to tick in the ruler designer. Every character in the world is measured against the prophecy continuously, their standing moves as marks are earned and lost, and the AI is competing for it too. Nine marks, and you never need all nine Dragon dreams, and greensight Born in salt and smoke, or beneath a bleeding star Hidden blood: a Valyrian bastard raised inside a great house Walking among the dead and surviving it Carrying spellforged steel Waking dragons from stone Dying, and not staying dead Five are decided at birth and four are earned. Two of them are checked continuously: lose the sword or the dragon and the claim goes with it. Read the Signs tells you which you carry, and costs nothing. And the realm decides what it means Deeds need validating by a red priest, a witch or a greenseer, since an unwitnessed miracle counts for nothing Two deeds make you Favored of R'hllor ; four make you Chosen (a game rule can make it one and three, or three and six) Lightbringer can be forged, at the price every version of the tale agrees on The man who ends it is called the Prince That Was Promised , the Dawnbringer if he did it with a Lightbringer he forged, or, failing both, the Dawn Kill the Night King and you are Azor Ahai Reborn , marks or no marks The AI plays all of it; rival claimants meet, and sometimes ally Lightbringer, once it is finally out of the third quench. Whether the one they named was ever the prince is decided behind the curtain, and the world only finds out at the end. There are four ways that can land.

The complete notes for every release, with reporter credits, are on the Workshop change-notes page and in the GitHub wiki . 1.1.3 — The Player Reports There is one Night King. Cast down by anything but a bane, he rises again within days in the same face and name, and every player is told so; dragon battle events can no longer pick him out of the line. Every dead lord now serves him, and no living ruler can fight on his side. The invasion's stages wait only on land he can attack, and wars on the Watch and the Iron Throne need more than held ground. Fixed: the freeze when the dead reach the Wall, Take the Black breaking your council, a Valyrian goblet becoming Lightbringer, Send for a Red Priest ignoring the priest already in your hall, raw trigger text under decisions, free folk resettling as feudal, and dead courts filling with thousands of new characters a year. A new rule asks a player in the North the Question of the North first. 1.1.2 — The Cold Does Not Fall The Night King no longer dies by accident: the commander pool, a lost dragon duel and the melee's own engine could all kill him outside a scene. The Others are no longer handed to the Iron Throne after a mega-war, and the dead no longer turn up as guests in living courts. Spanish and French added, with every line in all four languages. 1.1.1 — The Watch Keeps No Land A sworn brother renounces any land he inherits outside the Wall, the Lord Commander included; the exemption was how the Watch ended up holding a random county in the North. The dead answer to nobody living. Stannis gets Melisandre when he sends for a priest, and the lord of Dragonstone usually does. The Others cannot run schemes. Every county the dead take is set to full control so their own peasants never rise against them, and their land recovers control after a siege instead of never, which also stops the invasion stalling on its own revolts. The Crown of the Others no longer refuses its own king, and a load error on the house of the Others is gone. 1.1.0b — Keeping pace with A Game of Thrones A hotfix for AGOT's 0.5.2 hotfix. An invasion war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it, so held ground plus a won field closes a war inside a season instead of a second winter. The seventy-two named dragons look the way AGOT now paints them, a camp with a dragon in it cannot be moved beyond an intact Wall, and dragon eggs are held by the right people. 1.1.0a — One Host A hotfix, no new content. Nobody keeps an alliance with the dead, and the living no longer serve them. docs.x: Full disclosure You deserve to know what a submod touches, so here is the whole list. Every entry is a same-name override of exactly one AGOT definition: their body copied in full, one documented change, re-checked against their current version every release. It is longer than it used to be, because the mod is. Twenty definitions Six scripted rules : alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a character raised as one of the dead hands off to an heir), the second chance at a natural death (the red priest's last kiss), who may be a guest, who may be regent (never a sworn brother, never for a wight), and who may move a camp (ranging captains, like the First Ranger) Eight scripted triggers : knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead, and the Night King may lead his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than randomly slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never one of the dead), and one check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead cannot declare war on the dead) Four scripted effects : how rulers are named (wights, ranging captains, wardens and the Others get their titles; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), AGOT's dragon battle events (a dragon in battle cannot pick the Night King out of the line), and the melee's scene (snow, not a tourney ground) One decision, one casus belli : Restore the Night's Watch (refounded only when there is no Watch left), and the independence war (a sworn brother cannot secede from the Lord Commander) And two that merge rather than replace The ranger-camp domicile, so a ranging captain can hold a camp at all, and the Night's Watch title-gain handler, so appointing one doesn't force a government change on him. Everything else sits alongside AGOT rather than on top of it. The mod is safe to add and to update mid-save, though game rules are baked in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. Built on the work of others. This is a fork standing on Freeholder's original Long Night, Tehaen's 1.19 update, and Wepo94's The Long Night+.

docs.s: There is a door in this mod
docs.x: For the ones who read this far It has no handle on the outside. It opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once — at the moment your character first draws breath — and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. The riddle of the household ledger Three decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist . That is how it was built. Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house — and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives — not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. The door is checked once and never again, so a build that drifts into shape later will find nothing waiting. What's behind it: a household to put in order, a house to write down, and a ship that came back from somewhere ships do not come back from. The ship is the big one. It needs no console, no save editing and no downloads, only a character sheet built a particular way.

docs.x: Common questions Do I really have to disable the other Long Night mods? Yes, and it's the single most common cause of something being broken. This mod is a fork of both AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+, and it ships files at the same paths. Load order won't save you: either of them enabled anywhere in your playset overrides this mod with older code. They have to be disabled, not sorted lower. You can unsubscribe from them entirely. Do I need to start a new game? No. It's safe to add and to update mid-save. The one caveat is that CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created, so an existing campaign keeps whatever rules it started with. If you want to change the invasion timing or difficulty, that needs a fresh save. Does it work with Supernatural? Yes, with the compatibility patch. Load this mod, then Supernatural, then AGOT: Supernatural & The Long Night Compatibility Patch last. Supernatural has its own page here if you haven't seen it. What if I use other dragon mods? Pick them at campaign start and keep them. Dead dragons' appearances are stored against the exact set of portrait genes loaded at the time, so adding or removing any gene-adding mod mid-save can scramble dragons that have already died. Living dragons are unaffected. What version of CK3 is it for? CK3 1.19.0.6, built against the current release of A Game of Thrones. How do I actually kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once; that opens the War for the Dawn, which only an independent ruler can declare. Reach him, and the confrontation is the Last Hour: a Trial-of-Seven melee, you and your companions against him and his Walkers. Bring a bane. Dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down and the dark crowns another. Prowess counts for half against them, so a great swordsman with castle steel loses eventually. Bring companions, because losing has a worse outcome than dying: he raises you as one of his, and no priest can argue with that. What did 1.1.0 change? The ending. The Night King is fought on foot in a melee instead of rolled; lose and you are raised as an Other; White Walkers can be met during Winter Is Coming; the character page remembers the war; a rider can force a dragon over a standing Wall; and his host now grows with his conquest instead of arriving at full size. The 1.1.0a hotfix that followed stopped the dead declaring wars on each other and keeping allies among the living. The full notes are in What's changed below. Is it translated? English is complete. The Russian translation covers most of the mod; the newest events (the Last Hour, the encounter, the spear, consecration, travel danger) are still in English. Where do I report a bug or suggest something? The Long Night Discord is the fastest route: bug reports, ideas and questions all land there, and player input has driven a lot of what's in the mod. The Steam Workshop comments work too.

Each one links to the full section. How do I get resurrected? Do I have to do anything beforehand? Yes, and the order matters. Get a red priest into your court before you die , then take the free decision Ask for the Lord's Blessing . From then on, if you fall in a battle as a knight or commander, you get a card, your priest decides two days later, and if he pays you get a Get up button. Each priest can do it once in his life. There is a second road that needs no blessing: a red priest sitting as your court chaplain gives you a second chance at a natural death, if your faith can heal through the flames and the fire has a reason to want you. Neither road covers losing the Last Hour melee to the Night King; that ends in being taken. Full section. How do I kill the Night King? A stage that still cannot finish times out on its own: eight years beyond the Wall, four at the Wall, twenty in the North. docs.x: The questions that come up most, answered in a paragraph. Each one links to the full section. How do I get resurrected? Do I have to do anything beforehand? Yes, and the order matters. Get a red priest into your court before you die , then take the free decision Ask for the Lord's Blessing . From then on, if you fall in a battle as a knight or commander, you get a card, your priest decides two days later, and if he pays you get a Get up button. Each priest can do it once in his life. There is a second road that needs no blessing: a red priest sitting as your court chaplain gives you a second chance at a natural death, if your faith can heal through the flames and the fire has a reason to want you. Neither road covers losing the Last Hour melee to the Night King; that ends in being taken. Full section. How do I kill the Night King? Beat the dead in the field once so the War for the Dawn can be declared (independent rulers only), win a battle he is standing in, and take The Field Afterwards . Only dragonglass, Valyrian steel, Lightbringer or dragonfire destroy him; anything else casts him down, and within days he rises again, the same face and the same name. Form the line and fight the Last Hour with companions; lose it and he keeps you. Full section. Why has the Night King stalled after taking a region? The invasion moves in stages: beyond the Wall, then the Wall, then the North, then everywhere. Since 1.1.3 each stage waits only while someone he can attack still holds land in its region; before that, a lord he could not reach kept the gate shut. A stage that still cannot finish times out on its own: eight years beyond the Wall, four at the Wall, twenty in the North. He also never opens a new war while he is fighting one, and until 1.1.1 that included revolts by his own peasants. Full section. Do I have to disable the other Long Night mods? Yes. AGOT: The Long Night and The Long Night+ must be unchecked, not sorted below. This mod ships files at the same paths, so either of them anywhere in the playset overrides it with older code. Full section. What counts as a mark, and how many do I need? Nine marks exist. Five are decided at birth (dragon dreams, greensight, born in salt and smoke, born beneath a bleeding star, hidden blood), four are earned (equipped Valyrian steel, a dragon, surviving the dead, coming back from death). Two make you Favored and four make you Chosen under the default rule, and someone qualified has to say it: a red priest, a witch, or a greenseer. Full section.

docs.x: AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Developer Dlonem (Dlonem LLC) Game Crusader Kings III 1.19.0.6, with A Game of Thrones First release 8 August 2026 Current version 1.1.3 Steam Workshop 3780269495 Manual install Download without Steam Source GitHub Discord discord.gg/PTJzPQbqG7 Languages English, Russian, Spanish and French Lineage Fork of The Long Night+ (Wepo94), itself from The Long Night (Resurrected) (Tehaen), a port of AGOT: The Long Night (Freeholder) AGOT: The Long Night & Azor Ahai is a submod for A Game of Thrones , the Crusader Kings III total conversion. It builds the Long Night into a complete endgame: an undead invasion whose wights are named characters, a Night's Watch you can play from inside, the Wall coming down on camera, a melee against the Night King that you fight with the people who were actually there, and the Azor Ahai prophecy as a working mechanic that every character in the world is measured against. The invasion is a four-phase struggle you can watch coming for decades. When it arrives the Night King is a character with a court, a culture, a faith and a realm, and every lord he beats gets back up wearing his own face. Dragons that die over his ground come back on his side. The Wall falls at Castle Black. His host grows with what he takes, from twenty thousand beyond the Wall to two hundred thousand once the North is his. The living can take the black and mean it, send men and grain or their dungeons north, mine dragonglass, bring a red priest into the hall, forge Lightbringer at the price the tale demands, and, when the dead have been beaten once in the field, declare the War for the Dawn and go to him. This page is the reference and is kept current with the files. The mod page has the screenshots and the video; the Workshop page is the short version; the GitHub wiki carries the full changelog.

docs.x: When Winter Is Coming begins, the real length is rolled once: 12, 20, 28, 36 or 45 years (weights 15/25/30/20/10). Nothing in the interface shows the remaining time. The world can bite into it, never more than once every four years, never below five years remaining, and never below 60% of the original roll: a believed sighting takes four years (five when the AI believes one), a sacrifice to the Others six, a dead dragon three, a lost ranging or a snowstorm death two, choosing There is still summer in the south on the warning card two, and a Lord Commander's lost Great Ranging one. A new dragon gives four years back, up to the original roll. Every player gets Winter is Here on entering the phase, written for their own station: sworn brother, free folk, northman, dragonrider, red priest, lord, or nobody at all. When the clock runs out the invasion opens with one of five cards, chosen at random and with no effect on what follows: The Winds of Winter , A Dead Man in the Capital , A Ranging Returned , The Horror Beyond the Wall , or The True Enemy Revealed .

docs.s: The Night King and his host
docs.x: The Night King He is created at the Frigid Rise on the day the invasion opens: six to eight thousand years old, martial 25, intrigue 100, learning 65, prowess 30, carrying the traits Other and Great Other and the nickname the Night King . His title reads King Other 'the Night King' , with no number after the name. His culture is the Others (frostborn in the files), his faith the Cold Gods, his house the Others, his realm The Land of Always Winter , renamed The Long Night once he holds thirty counties. He takes the hegemony and fifteen counties beyond the Wall on day one, is made independent, and receives the Crown of the Others and the Crystal Sword. He leads his host in person. One of the Others is always his named heir: the best sword in his court, a man first. If he is cast down, that heir takes the crown and rises in his place with his face, his name and the whole kit, so to everyone watching the Night King has simply got back up (1.1.3), and killing him with ordinary steel does not leave the dead weaker. His culture cannot be reasoned with: the dead learn nothing (their innovations are Bronze Age and never advance), keep no mercenaries, buy nothing, and have every county opinion at +400 so nothing of theirs ever revolts. The Night King's court is sixty-two elite Others, and every ten days it is re-sacrificed: frostborn courtiers are made Others, everyone else and every prisoner dies. Since 1.1.1 the Others, the Night King and wights cannot run hostile or personal schemes at all. How big his host is Two forces. The elite host is fixed: ten thousand of The Dead (damage 38, toughness 75, siege tier 4) plus trebuchets, needing no supply. The Risen Dead horde (damage 3, toughness 25, counters peasant militia, costs him nothing to keep) is a milestone top-up, refilled every thirty days up to four regiments at a time: Milestone Standard target Weak ×0.75 Strong ×1.25 Insane ×1.5 The invasion opens 20,000 15,000 25,000 30,000 Everything beyond the Wall is his 50,000 37,500 62,500 75,000 Castle Black has fallen 100,000 75,000 125,000 150,000 The North is done 200,000 150,000 250,000 300,000 140 counties or more 250,000 187,500 312,500 375,000 The hard cap is 500,000, the population of King's Landing. Both units fight better in winter. docs.x: Every thirty days the invasion looks for a neighbouring independent ruler to attack. Small neighbours (AI, under four counties, below empire tier) are absorbed by fealty rather than war, even while he is busy; anyone bigger, or any player, gets a war. The invasion does not start a new war while it is fighting one, and it takes a pause between wars (the table above). Targets follow a ladder of stage gates, each with a clock that fails open so a gate can never stall the invasion for good: Beyond the Wall first. While the Wall stands and a neighbour he can attack still holds land beyond the Wall, or unclaimed wilderness up there is still being absorbed (one county every thirty days), only holders of land beyond the Wall qualify. Eight-year window. Then the Wall. While Castle Black stands, only a ruler seated at or holding land on the Wall. Four-year window, refilled by four years each time the Watch beats the dead from a Wall seat. The Wall is the climax, enforced. Then the North. Once Castle Black has fallen, only holders of land in the North, until no neighbour he can attack holds any of it. Twenty-year window. Then everywhere. Inside the North the front marches rather than jumps: a target outside the North is illegal while any living northern March still borders the dead, and Winterfell's crown is illegal while any other northern March stands. Every great house's seat is a Last Bastion during Winter Is Coming and the Long Night (+3 fort level, +50% garrison, +8 defender advantage), and the target picker walks around bastions until the seat's own duchy is half in dead hands; a crown's seat is admitted only once the dead hold two kingdom titles or ten counties in that empire. Until 1.1.3 a region held by someone the Night King could not reach as a top liege, such as a northern county whose lord answers to a southern king, kept that stage's gate armed until its window lapsed. That was the mechanism behind "he took the North and stopped". Since 1.1.3 each stage asks the same question the target search does, so land he cannot attack no longer holds a gate, and the host's milestones follow the same answer. The windows stay as a backstop and run once per Long Night: a Night King who is cast down and rises again does not restart them.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: The casus belli is Seize All Occupied Lands , and the war is called The Long Night . The War Tier rule picks the size of the bite: March (the default) takes one kingdom-tier March at a time, or a duchy from a smaller victim; Duchy always takes one duchy; Empire sweeps whole realms. Occupation counts for war score with the defender's capital weighted; since 1.1.0b a war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it, and the score climbs on its own from there so held ground plus a won field closes a war inside a season. Since 1.1.3, in a March or Empire war occupation alone can carry at most three quarters of the bar and the climb waits six months into the war, so the Watch and the Iron Throne are no longer beaten before anyone has fought. Duchy wars, which is every war beyond the Wall, are unchanged. When he wins, the war goal transfers in full and any other occupied county transfers only if it connects to land the dead already hold; the rest is given back, and allies' land is never taken. On Standard and above extra bordering duchies come with the goal (table above), never a bastion. When he loses, the invasion pauses for the re-arm period, he pays reparations, and the world remembers: the War for the Dawn can only be declared once the dead have lost a war , or once the Night King has been cast down in the field. The dead have no friends. No alliance survives with one of them on either side, no living knight, councillor, court official or commander serves them, any dead lord standing outside the Night King's realm is sworn to him (1.1.3; before that such lords were made independent, which left realms of the dead he never took back), no living ruler can fight on their side of a war (a company, a paid ally or a hired sword is removed the moment it joins, and the Night King's living tributaries are released), the dead never declare war on the dead, and every county that comes into dead hands is set to full control on the day it arrives (1.1.1), so his own peasants never rise against him.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: The Wall comes down when the dead take Castle Black: the Watch is at war with the Night King and he holds the county, or Castle Black is already in dead hands. Every player gets the cinematic The Wall Has Fallen , and the middle section of the Wall breaks on the map. A fifth of every black brother flees south; sworn brothers who held castles keep them, and the rest are released from their vows as they go and pooled at Winterfell, Karhold and the Last Hearth, so Castle Black no longer pulls them back (1.1.3). Castle Black takes The Wall Is Broken (−15 county opinion, −20% development growth, −15% supply). Thirty days later comes The Age of Heroes Is Ended , opening in your own station: sworn brother, free folk, blood of the dragon, northman, red priest, lord, or nobody. It writes the memory alive when the Wall fell . Thirty days after that Castle Black is ruined, the North stage of the invasion opens, and the horde's next milestone unlocks. The moment the dead hold any county on the Wall, the ward is gone: living dragons can fight beyond the Wall without the penalty, and the +60 the spear gets against a dragon forced over an intact Wall is removed. If the living retake the Wall, the ward returns. Under The Cycle , the Wall is raised again in the next Long Summer. Once the Long Night arrives, Black Cloaks at Your Gates can reach dukes and up across the Seven Kingdoms (never Dorne, the Reach or the Stormlands): real survivors from the Wall first, one stranger if the list is empty. Take them in and up to three join you, free of their vows, followed by What the Watch Left You , which can put Black Cloaks on the Walls on your realm for twenty years (+5% garrison, +5% reinforcement, +2 advantage).

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: Who gets raised Dying is not the trigger; being taken into the dead's realm is . Anyone who gains a title from one of the dead, any vassal they gain, every courtier of an Other, and every living person in the Night King's service is converted, along with their court. Before it happens a landless noble may flee (a base 15% chance, more if craven, less if brave), and a landed lord may flee south as a refugee of the Dawn (base 10%), which is also the Flee South decision offered to any lord the dark is coming for. The dead keep no vows: a sworn brother or silent sister raised without a title of his or her own loses the vows (1.1.3). A wight keeps his face, his titles and his realm, now under the Risen Thrall government, which is unplayable by design: a player who is raised hands off to an heir. The trait Wight makes him tireless (health +50, immortal, incapacitated, cannot marry or have children, no inheritance), hated (−150 general opinion) and dreaded (+25). Every alliance, friendship, love and marriage he had is severed, and his spouse gets Death Did Us Part . Close family, friends and lovers who are players get A Face I Know when someone they knew rises. A wight is never promoted to an Other. The Night King's own kill is different. Lose the Last Hour to him and you are raised as an Other , not a wight, with the Other trait, the house of the Others and the flag that puts you on his side of the line the next time a champion reaches him. A landed champion stays landed in the dead's host. When the Night King is destroyed, every wight and every risen dragon dies where it stands, every living member of the house of the Others is gone save one (see the Cycle ), and the land the dead held is scoured. Undead dragons Under the default rule, They Raise Their Kills , the Others are given nothing. docs.x: Dying is not the trigger; being taken into the dead's realm is . Anyone who gains a title from one of the dead, any vassal they gain, every courtier of an Other, and every living person in the Night King's service is converted, along with their court. Before it happens a landless noble may flee (a base 15% chance, more if craven, less if brave), and a landed lord may flee south as a refugee of the Dawn (base 10%), which is also the Flee South decision offered to any lord the dark is coming for. The dead keep no vows: a sworn brother or silent sister raised without a title of his or her own loses the vows (1.1.3). A wight keeps his face, his titles and his realm, now under the Risen Thrall government, which is unplayable by design: a player who is raised hands off to an heir. The trait Wight makes him tireless (health +50, immortal, incapacitated, cannot marry or have children, no inheritance), hated (−150 general opinion) and dreaded (+25). Every alliance, friendship, love and marriage he had is severed, and his spouse gets Death Did Us Part . Close family, friends and lovers who are players get A Face I Know when someone they knew rises. A wight is never promoted to an Other. The Night King's own kill is different. Lose the Last Hour to him and you are raised as an Other , not a wight, with the Other trait, the house of the Others and the flag that puts you on his side of the line the next time a champion reaches him. A landed champion stays landed in the dead's host. When the Night King is destroyed, every wight and every risen dragon dies where it stands, every living member of the house of the Others is gone save one (see the Cycle ), and the land the dead held is scoured.

The Road Is Not Empty is wights: ride through them (a prowess test, 55% clean), form a line and get a fire going (80% they burn, 20% they burn and so does one of yours), or leave the wagons and ride. docs.x: The Watch's realm is renamed The Night's Watch . Nineteen castles on the Wall, eight ranging companies with camps on the map, a Lord Commander with decisions nobody else gets, and a set of rules that keep the Watch out of southern politics whether it likes it or not. Taking the black The decision is Take the Black . It is open to any adult man standing in the Seven Kingdoms who is not free folk, not a maester or septon, not already a sworn brother and not one of the dead, while a Lord Commander exists and a ranging company is free (vacant, or held by an AI captain he can stand down). You need somewhere for the realm to go: an heir, a liege, or nothing to give up. There is no prestige requirement. Women are refused at the gate. What it costs is the oath: every title you hold passes to your primary heir, or to your liege if you have none, with no claim kept; your marriage, betrothal, claims, debts, Iron Bank shares and Kingsguard place end at the Wall; any dragon that answers to you is unbonded; any adventurer company you led is disbanded. Your successor remembers it (+40 opinion for sixty years), your family and former vassals think better of you for it, and your close family moves to the heir's court. Since 1.1.3 your old council is dismissed, courtiers fit for the black take it with you and most of the rest go their own way, and a sworn brother joins your camp so the four ranger seats can be filled. What you get is a ranging company of your own, sworn to the Lord Commander, and you play on as the brother. The eight ranging companies The companies are The Long Ranging, The Deep Ranging, The Cold Ranging, The Silent Ranging, The Black Ranging, The Winter Ranging, The Far Ranging and The Last Ranging . Each is a landless title under the Wall with a real camp on the map, a captain titled Ranger-Captain , and its own government, Ranging Company : army upkeep −60%, men-at-arms upkeep −70%, +2 martial and +2 prowess per prestige level, +0.5 monthly dread, and no holy orders. The camp is the ranger camp AGOT gives the First Ranger, opened to all eight companies, and it can only be pitched on the Wall or beyond it, never with raised armies. From game start each company has a historical northman captain, and a new captain every generation, all the way to 8320. A captain can March the Ranging to Craster's Keep, Whitetree or Hardhome and Return to the Wall ; the camp travels, provisions are topped up at the Wall, and the arrival is quiet by design. Once a year, if the Lord Commander's court holds ten or more brothers who could be posted, each company with fewer than six ranging brothers gets one, weighted toward rangers, the brave and the strong. Captains compete for First Ranger : when the holder dies, an AI captain is chosen (martial and prowess of 12 or more, the ranger lifestyle and bravery all count) and moves to that seat; player captains are not drafted into it. Under the default rule the Watch fills companies one through five itself and holds three open for players; Leave Them for Players leaves a dead captain's seat waiting; All Eight Ride keeps every company manned. When a captain dies, the company passes to a qualifying brother of the Lord Commander's court, or a ranger is created for it, or the Lord Commander holds it himself. A ranger who has been sworn long enough (a hundred points of the Night's Watch trait; a recruit does not get given a castle) can Ask for a Castle and trade the company for a keepership. Call the Great Ranging (Winter Is Coming or the Long Night, 100 prestige, one at a time, a year between) sends two hundred brothers north. Send them for word and the odds are 40% Word From the North (the warning that unlocks dragonglass, plus prestige and learning), 35% The Ranging Is Lost (four catalyst points, the dark a year closer), 25% They Came Back Quiet (a courtier dead of cold, the dark a year closer, but the word arrives). Lead it yourself for 150 prestige and the odds become 55/30/15. Send a Brother Recruiting rides a sworn brother of your court south. docs.x: Send Men and Grain to the Wall is open to landed rulers who are northmen, kings, or who have heard the warning, once every five years: a cart of grain (100 gold; +25 Lord Commander opinion, +50 piety, +25 prestige), a season's stores (500; +50, +120, +60), or empty the vaults (1,500; +75, +250, +120). The gold goes straight to the Lord Commander, the realm's ledger goes up by one, two or three, and the Watch's petitions pay out more once the ledger reaches three and again at eight. Emptying the vaults is remembered if you later take the black yourself. Send the Prisoners to the Wall empties your cells in one order. Every prisoner who can take the black goes, as a sworn brother and not as an offer he can refuse, and the decision names a reason for each one who cannot: women, children, free folk, the dead, independent rulers, house heads, the last of a house, and, under the default rule, anyone above county rank. The Tier Ceiling rule can lift that last one so a king can end his days a sworn brother. You gain 100 piety and the Lord Commander's gratitude.

docs.x: A sworn brother who inherits land outside the Wall renounces it ( The Watch Takes No Part ): the title goes to its de jure liege, or the next lawful hand, never to another brother or one of the dead.
