docs.x: Mine the Dragonglass appears in Winter Is Coming or the Long Night for any ruler, landless included, who has a reason to know: he heard the warning, looked north, is a sworn brother, has greensight, or the Long Night is simply here. It costs 200 gold plus 200 for each tier above count (a quarter off if you studied the glass, never less than 150) and gives thirty years of Dragonglass Stores , which counts as a bane at the Last Hour and opens the dragonglass option in the melee. Six sites of dragonglass lore, Castle Black and the Fist of the First Men among them, can be visited on a journey. Send for a Red Priest (150 gold) is for a landed adult who is an interloper in the struggle, a player whose faith or culture already counts as involved, or a follower of R'hllor without a priest, and who has a reason to believe: the faith, Valyrian blood, the warning, greensight, or being Stannis or the lord of Dragonstone. A priest arrives in four to thirteen months with The Priest at the Gate . Stannis gets Melisandre if she is free; a Baratheon lord of Dragonstone gets her three times in four; everyone else has a one-in-ten chance of Melisandre or Thoros of Myr, weighted by prophecy deeds, and otherwise a Myrish priest is created for you. If a red priest is already in your hall, serving in any seat or visiting as a guest, the decision becomes Hear the Red Priest instead: free, and the card comes the next day with that priest on it (1.1.3). At the gate you can take the red ( Then your god is my god , which makes an interloper involved in the Long Night, takes the priest's own faith when he follows the red god so he can serve as your chaplain afterwards, and costs 200 piety and 100 prestige), keep your steel and keep the priest, or burn him. A red priest, once he is your court chaplain, is what names you, blesses you, and brings you back.

docs.x: A red priest can spend himself on one person, once, ever. There are two roads back and both need the priest in place before you die. What you must do beforehand Have a red priest. He needs the Red Priest trait, to be an available adult, to have at least a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and to have never given the last kiss. Get one with Send for a Red Priest , or appoint any R'hllor courtier as court chaplain and AGOT gives him the trait. Take Ask for the Lord's Blessing. It is free, has no cooldown and no faith requirement. It is shown whenever a priest who can bless you is within reach: your court chaplain, a ranging company's camp priest, or any courtier or guest. You cannot take it while imprisoned or while another priest's words already stand over you. The priest can also offer it to you himself ( Offer the Lord's Blessing ); refusing him costs him piety. Either way The Words Are Said . Keep him alive and unspent. If your priest dies, the bond is released and you can ask another. If he spends his one kiss on someone else, he is spent forever and you are free to ask again. Ask again after any change of priest. Give the fire a reason. The priest's answer is not automatic (see below). Being Favored or Chosen, having even one prophecy mark, or fighting in Winter Is Coming or the Long Night makes him far likelier to pay; being his friend makes refusal rare. Falling in battle With the blessing on you, the day you fall in a battle as a knight or a commander you are wounded instead of killed and carry Fell in the Dark (health −1.5, prowess −4). The next day you get You Do Not Get Up . Two days later your priest, wherever he is, gets Send For Me, Whatever Is Left : he pays ( Take it out of me, then. Not him. ) or refuses ( Not this one. R'hllor forgive me, not this one. ). His odds to pay are 70 against 30 to refuse as a base; being worth the fire adds 50 to paying and, if you are not, 60 to refusing; friendship adds 40 to paying and cuts refusal to a fifth. If he pays, a day later you get The Fire Gave You Back , and the Get up button is the resurrection. If he refuses, The Fire Kept What It Had arrives and its only option kills you. You have to survive the three days in between; if your wounds take you first he cannot pay. Whether your death lands in this pool at all is a weighted draw against the game's own battle deaths: base 40 as a knight and 8 as a commander, halved outside the cold, half again more in the Long Night and for a champion of R'hllor. Then The Last Kiss fires the next day. This route costs 150 piety as well. docs.x: The Last Hour melee. Losing to the Night King there is not a death the fire can argue with; you are taken and raised as an Other. docs.x: Since 1.1.0 the Night King is fought, not rolled. Reaching him The War for the Dawn can only be declared once the dead have lost a war or the Night King has been cast down in the field, and only by an independent ruler holding a county or more, with a thousand men and a dynasty of some standing; vassals march to their liege's war, and anyone can join one already running. The Iron Throne declares it if it is held, and everyone else joins. It has no white peace, and losing it costs 500 prestige and gives him five years' respite. The decision reads: The War for the Dawn cannot be declared while the Others savor a recent victory. Three roads lead to a scene. Win a battle he is standing in, as commander or knight, and the winning commander gets The Field Afterwards two days later. Win the War for the Dawn on score and the worthiest attacker, or the worthiest knight among them, gets The Last Hour with him on the field. Imprison him and his captor, or the worthiest of the captor's knights and courtiers, gets the same card with him in chains. Worthiness is the prophecy's arithmetic plus prowess, minus wounds, and a man carrying a bane outranks everyone who is not. The Field Afterwards The card reads differently depending on what you brought: Lightbringer, Dawn, a dragon overhead, Valyrian steel, dragonglass, a dragon the dead took from you, nothing at all. The choices: End it. A single duel against him. Shown greyed if you carry nothing that can hurt him. docs.x: The War for the Dawn can only be declared once the dead have lost a war or the Night King has been cast down in the field, and only by an independent ruler holding a county or more, with a thousand men and a dynasty of some standing; vassals march to their liege's war, and anyone can join one already running. The Iron Throne declares it if it is held, and everyone else joins. It has no white peace, and losing it costs 500 prestige and gives him five years' respite. The decision reads: The War for the Dawn cannot be declared while the Others savor a recent victory. Three roads lead to a scene. Win a battle he is standing in, as commander or knight, and the winning commander gets The Field Afterwards two days later. Win the War for the Dawn on score and the worthiest attacker, or the worthiest knight among them, gets The Last Hour with him on the field. Imprison him and his captor, or the worthiest of the captor's knights and courtiers, gets the same card with him in chains. Worthiness is the prophecy's arithmetic plus prowess, minus wounds, and a man carrying a bane outranks everyone who is not.

docs.x: Four things: dragonglass (mined stores, an armed knight, or having studied the glass), Valyrian steel (a Valyrian blade: a sword, axe, spear or dagger, never a bow, armour or a goblet), Lightbringer (forged or consecrated), or dragonfire (a living dragon of yours over the field, which beyond an intact Wall means one you forced across). A won melee with ordinary steel or a stray battle death casts him down, and a War for the Dawn won on score with nobody fit to face him leaves him standing (1.1.3). Cast down, he rises again within days: his named heir, always one of the Others, takes the crown, his face, his name and every bonus, and every player gets He Is Not Destroyed , which says what would have ended him. A dragon in the press of an ordinary battle does not count, and since 1.1.3 AGOT's dragon battle events cannot pick him out of the line at all. Casting him down does still count as beating the dead, so it opens the War for the Dawn. Under the War for the Dawn resolution rule even a bane is not enough until that war is won, and the Field Afterwards and the Last Hour only open while a War for the Dawn against him is running. When a bane lands, whoever landed it is Azor Ahai Reborn , marks or no marks, named or not. If a dragon did it, its rider takes the deed. An unnamed nobody can end the Long Night and prove every red priest in the world wrong.

docs.x: Six to ten days after the kill, every player gets The Dawn , and the text is the only place the hidden coin is ever read. If the prophecy was true and the slayer was named: it was prophecy, and it was always going to be. If it was false and he was named: the faith will remember this as the night it was proved right, and it was not. If it was true and nobody named him: the flames never lied, and nobody ever learned to read them. If it was false and nobody named him: he was just a man, and that will have to be enough. If a wild dragon did it and no one can be named: it ended, which is the only part anyone can prove. The trait, the modifier and the nickname do not depend on the coin. The slayer is called the Dawnbringer if he forged Lightbringer and killed with it, the Prince That Was Promised if he was named or has the blood of the dragon, and the Dawn otherwise, with 10,000 dynasty prestige, 2,000 prestige and 1,000 piety. A month later The Men Who Were There names the three who stood in the front rank, from the melee's real line: each is knighted if he was not already, gains 5,000 dynasty prestige and the memory. If you went alone, the record says so. At four months The Reckoning asks whether you write it down.

docs.x: If a hundred years pass in the Long Night with the Night King alive and holding sixty counties or more, the dark has won. Every player gets The Long Defeat , he takes The Dark Won , and the struggle ends. After any won battle against the dead, Someone You Knew can show you a face on the other side.

docs.x: During Winter Is Coming, before the dead have taken a single county, a player who is a sworn brother, or standing at the Wall or beyond it, or whose capital is in the North, has a 15% chance each pulse (with four years between) of Something on the Ridge (a sighting, seven times in ten) or The Snow Stands Up (three in ten): one White Walker of prowess 16 against you and a party of one to five, real men first and created rangers to fill. Win, and It Came Apart : 500 prestige, the memory slew one of the Others , and at three kills the modifier Slayer of White Walkers (+10 dread, +0.3 monthly prestige). Lose, and it is 40% You Do Not Stop Running (your companions die, you are wounded), 45% The Cold Closes (everyone dies, you are taken by the dead), 15% It Lets One Live , the Sam Tarly outcome: the weakest real companion is spared and everyone else, you included, is not.

docs.x: Nobody is born Azor Ahai. You accumulate marks, someone qualified says the name out loud, and then you have to go and do it. Forge Lightbringer is open to any champion of R'hllor (Favored, Chosen, Azor Ahai Reborn or Returned) in Winter Is Coming or the Long Night, with a hall of his own and a red priest or a court smith at hand, for 300 gold plus 200 per tier above count. The third ( A Hundred Days ) asks: your spouse or someone who loves you dies on the anvil for the full sword (+30 dread, 300 piety, 200 prestige, your close family will never forgive it); a zealous volunteer of your faith gives a lesser sword; a man who has already died once can put it through his own chest for the full sword and a hole that never heals; or you put the hammer down and keep the forge for another day. Consecrate the Blade (150 gold) stamps a Valyrian blade you have equipped (a sword, axe, spear or dagger; since 1.1.3 never armour, a bow or a goblet) as Lightbringer at the same price, or, if the blade is Dawn and its bearer was born beneath the bleeding star, at no life at all. Someone has to say the words: a red priest as your court chaplain or camp priest, or you, if you are one. The blade keeps its own name and history. A save where armour or a goblet was consecrated before 1.1.3 has it unmade once, and the world may make a Lightbringer again. Lightbringer Effects Full +12 prowess, +3 advantage, +2 piety a month, +20 same-faith and +10 general opinion, +10 dread, +10% dynasty prestige, +15% martial experience Lesser +7 prowess, +2 advantage, +1 piety a month, +12 same-faith and +5 general opinion, +10% martial experience Consecrated blade Its own stats, plus +2 prowess, +1 advantage, +1.5 piety a month, +15 same-faith and +5 general opinion, +8 dread Whoever carries it bears a bane at the Last Hour, gets the strongest bonus in the melee, and, if he forged it and kills with it, is called the Dawnbringer .

docs.x: A lord of another faith with a red priest in his hall, or who has been named, or who has heard the warning, has a one-in-five chance once in his life of A Colder Kind of Doubt , which leads to The Nightfire and Take the Red . Converting costs 200 piety and 100 prestige and twenty years of your vassals and clergy thinking less of you. The other door is at the priest's arrival: Then your god is my god , which also swears you to the Dawn.

docs.x: Under the default rule a coin is flipped at game start and hidden forever; the other two rules fix it. It is read exactly once, at the reveal, and it changes nothing but what the world believes it saw. You can do everything right, be named by every priest in Westeros, and find out you were never him.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: When the Night King is destroyed, the land the dead held is scoured : the seat of a kingdom becomes a renowned great ruin, the seat of a duchy a sizeable ruin, everything else wilderness. Only counties the mod scoured are ever touched; Harrenhal and the old ruins are left alone. Twenty, thirty or forty-five years later each scoured ruin that nobody has reclaimed becomes wilderness too, so AGOT's own settlement decision can take it. Every player gets A Dream of Spring . The Question of the North goes, under the default rule, to a player first: a player on the Iron Throne, then a player holding the North, then the highest-ranked player with land in the North. If no player qualifies, or under the rule's Crown option, it goes to the Iron Throne, or an independent King in the North, or the greatest independent crown left standing. It comes within six months: The Watch shall rise again refounds the Night's Watch under a new Lord Commander with the Wall's castles and 500 gold (or reinforces it, if it held), and the free folk are never welcomed south; Let the free folk come south renames the Wall's kingdom the Giftlands and settles it clan by clan, up to two clans a year, as vassals of the crown, and the Watch never rises again. The choice is permanent, even under the Cycle. Lords who fled south as refugees of the Dawn can Return North : a settler caravan with 1,000 provisions and 150 gold, staged up the Kingsroad through King's Landing, the Inn at the Crossroads and Moat Cailin, to their lost seat if it is empty or the nearest empty land. Free folk settle as tribal clans (1.1.3); anyone else takes his culture head's government. Rebuilding the ancestral seat is worth 200 prestige and Restored the Ancestral Seat for life. A refugee with a dragon can instead Return With Fire and settle the question of who holds his hall; there are four ways that goes and only one of them is quiet. The crown can Sell Colonization Rights to Essos , 150 gold a coastal county to a Braavosi, Pentoshi, Myrish, Tyroshi, Lyseni or Volantene lord, once every eighteen months, and every northern vassal remembers it for ten years. With Iron Throne Reformation on, every independent ruler in the Seven Kingdoms is asked The Future of the Seven Kingdoms : swear fealty to the Iron Throne, or remain independent. Under The Cycle , the Dawn lasts five years and flows back into the Long Summer with the ledger wiped, the Wall raised again and Castle Black repaired, a new summer target rolled, and one thing kept: a Night's Queen survives the cleanup to seed the next wave. Waves two and three carry The Dead Remember (+2 levy size, +3 advantage, +10% toughness), four and five Centuries of Winter (+4, +6, +20% toughness, +10% damage, four knights), six and up The Last Long Night (+7, +10, +35% toughness, +25% damage, eight knights, +25% knight effectiveness). Everyone who stood in the front rank at the last Dawn, and Azor Ahai Reborn, carries Saw the First Dawn when the next night opens, and gets You Have Seen This Before .

docs.x: Fourteen rules, all under the AGOT heading, all baked in when a save is created. Defaults are marked. Rule Options The Long Night Chance default Certain (guaranteed) · Near-Certain (75%) · Even Odds (50%) · Remote Odds (25%) · No Chance. One roll, for the first Long Night; a "no" world never accrues summer points, and under The Cycle every later wave comes regardless. The Long Night Moment default A Random Summer (never sooner than 25 years, usually 90 to 130, sometimes far later) · Immediately · In Fifty Years · In One-Hundred Years · In One Hundred-Fifty Years · Full Random (30 years to over two centuries, no cap) · Historical (from a start before 255 AC the Long Night lands between about 280 and 320 AC; from 255 AC or later the game opens in Winter Is Coming and it arrives by 300 AC; either way only if the Chance rule lets it) · Manual (only the Trigger the Long Night decision starts it, every wave is called the same way, the decision is hidden during a Dawn, and the tracker stays empty by design). The Long Night Strength Weak · default Standard · Strong · Insane. See the strength table . The Long Night Resolution default Death (the Long Night ends the moment the Night King is destroyed) · War for the Dawn (killing him is not enough; any death before the war is won casts him down, and he rises again). The Long Night War Tier Duchy (slow grind) · default March (recommended; Winterfell only once the North has gone quiet) · Empire (rapid onslaught). The Long Night Ice Dragon default They Raise Their Kills · One Simply Appears · Off. The Question of the North default A Player in the North First (a player on the Iron Throne, then a player holding the North, then the highest-ranked player with land in the North) · The Crown (the AI crown decides, as before 1.1.3). The Long Night Iron Throne Reformation default On (kingdom-tier rulers are offered fealty to the Iron Throne after the Dawn) · Off. The Long Night Recurrence default Once · The Cycle (the Long Night comes back, heavier each time; the Moment rule sets the gap). Send the Prisoners Tier Ceiling default Counts and Below · Any Rank (the King of the Iron Throne can end his days a sworn brother). Azor Ahai — Was There Ever a Prince? default Let the Flames Decide (a hidden coin) · There Is a Prince · There Is No Prince. Azor Ahai — Naming Claimants default As the Books Have It (two and four marks) · The Flames Are Loud (one and three) · The Citadel's Reading (three and six) · Nobody Is Ever Named. Azor Ahai — Who May Be Named default Anyone at All · Players Only · One at a Time (at most one living Chosen; the seat reopens when they stop breathing). The Ranging Companies default The Watch Recruits (never more than five; three companies held for players) · Leave Them for Players · All Eight Ride.

docs.x: Compatible with AGOT+, Valyrian Steel, Submod Core, Nobility of Westeros, Essos Expanded, Legacy of Valyria, AGOT Additional Models and Special Buildings, Seasons of Ice and Fire, and anything else that names its own rulers. Supernatural needs the compatibility patch, last in the list. Essos Expanded and Legacy of Valyria are untested and unsupported; keep them above this mod. Legacy of Valyria ships its own versions of three rules this mod overrides, including the one that is the whole entry point to resurrection, so this mod must load after it. Every override is one AGOT or vanilla definition, copied in full, with one documented change, re-checked against the current AGOT build every release: Six scripted rules: alliances (nothing living keeps an alliance with the dead), who may be played (a raised player hands off to an heir; a landed sworn brother is playable), the second chance at death (the last kiss), who may be a guest (not the Others), who may be regent (a sworn brother only for a sworn brother), who may move a camp (ranging captains, and no dragon beyond an intact Wall). Eight scripted triggers: knights, court positions, councillors and commanders (the living do not serve the dead; the Night King leads his own host), capture (he is imprisoned rather than slain in a siege), regency for personal reasons, who may become a landless adventurer (never the dead), and the check thirteen AGOT casus belli share (the dead do not declare war on the dead). Four scripted effects: how rulers are titled (wights, captains, the wilderness and the Others get their names; every other mod's titles pass straight through), what happens when a dragon dies in a dragon duel (the dead may claim it), AGOT's dragon battle events (a dragon in battle cannot pick the Night King out of the line), and the melee's scene. One decision, one casus belli, three files: Restore the Night's Watch (hidden once the Question has been asked), the independence war (nobody secedes from the Watch), the ranger-camp domicile (opened to eight companies), the peasant faction (never against a wight), and the portrait animations (five wight poses). Languages: English, Russian, Spanish and French, with every line present in all four. English is the author's; the Spanish and French are a first pass, and corrections are welcome. Large playsets are worth one look at logs/database_conflicts.log .

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: There is a door in this mod. It has no handle on the outside, it opens for one kind of lord, it is checked exactly once, at the moment your character first draws breath, and nobody has ever stumbled into it by accident. Four decisions sit behind it. They do not appear greyed out with their requirements listed; if you are not the one it is waiting for, they do not exist. The riddle of the household ledger Everything you need is below. Nothing below is a lie. Found your own house, and answer to no one above you. Take the sin the septons put in the flesh, and the virtue they put in the work. Both. They sit oddly together. That is rather the point. Then set your sword-arm at three fives , not one more, and not one less. Do all of it in the ruler designer, before the first snow. The door is checked once and never again, so a build that drifts into shape later will find nothing waiting. What's behind it: a household to put in order, a house to write down, a physician worth the name, and a ship that came back from somewhere ships do not come back from. The ship is the big one. No console, no save editing, no downloads. Just a character sheet built a particular way.

docs.t: The Long Night & Azor Ahai Wiki — every mechanic on one page
docs.x: My priest refused to bring me back. Why? He rolls. The base is 70 to pay against 30 to refuse; if you are not worth the fire (no champion trait, no mark, not fighting in the cold) refusal gets +60, and if you are his friend refusal is cut to a fifth. Make him your friend, earn a mark, and ask again with a fresh priest next time. If the card said there was only ever one of it to give, your priest had already spent his kiss on someone else. I have a red priest but the blessing decision does not show. Check that he is an adult, available (not travelling, not imprisoned), has a first level of devotion or a learning of 10, and has never given the last kiss. Then check that nobody else's blessing already stands over you; the decision tells you if it does. I died and nothing happened. Only battle deaths as a knight or commander, and natural deaths with a red priest as your chaplain, can be argued with. Duels, executions, the Last Hour melee and scripted deaths never can. Battle deaths are also a weighted draw against the game's own, so the blessing raises your odds rather than guaranteeing the card. The Night King took the North and stopped. Before 1.1.3 the North stage waited on every northern county, including ones held by a vassal of a southern king, which he cannot target, until its twenty-year window ran out. Since 1.1.3 it waits only while someone he can attack still holds land in the North, so he moves on as soon as that stops being true. He also never opens a new war while fighting one; before 1.1.1 his own peasant revolts counted, which is fixed. Can I be Lord Commander? Election is AGOT's and the mod does not change who is eligible. A sworn brother holding a castle is playable, and a player Lord Commander who dies passes play to a landed brother of his family. Can a woman take the black? No. The Watch is brothers only, at the gate and in the dungeons order. Does killing him with ordinary steel do anything? It casts him down: within days he rises again, the same face, the same name and the same bonuses, every player gets the card He Is Not Destroyed , and the Long Night goes on. It does count as beating the dead, so it opens the War for the Dawn, and you are remembered as the Undaunted. Can I change the rules on an existing save? No. CK3 bakes game rules in when a save is created. Timing, strength, the prophecy coin and the rest need a fresh campaign. Where do I report a bug? The Long Night Discord is fastest; GitHub issues work too. Include your CK3 version, your full load order, and whether you are on the Workshop copy or a manual install.

docs.x: Version What it did 1.1.3 — The Player Reports One Night King: cast down by anything but a bane, he rises again in the same face and name, a card tells every player so, and dragon battle events can no longer take him. Every dead lord serves him and no living ruler fights on his side. The invasion's stages wait only on land he can attack, and wars on the Watch and the Iron Throne need more than held ground. The freeze at the Wall, the Take the Black council crash, a Valyrian goblet that could become Lightbringer, Send for a Red Priest missing the priest already in your hall, raw trigger text in decisions, free folk turning feudal, and dead courts filling with thousands of new characters a year are fixed. New rule: The Question of the North asks a player first. 1.1.2 — The Cold Does Not Fall He no longer dies by accident: the commander pool, a lost dragon duel and the melee's own engine could kill him outside a scene. The Others are no longer handed to the Iron Throne after a mega-war, and the dead no longer visit living courts as guests. Spanish and French added. 1.1.1 The Watch keeps no land: a sworn brother, the Lord Commander included, renounces anything he inherits outside the Wall. The dead answer to nobody living. Stannis gets Melisandre and Dragonstone usually does. The Others cannot scheme. Every county the dead take is set to full control, so their own peasants never rise, and their land recovers control after a siege instead of never. The Crown of the Others no longer refuses its own king. A load error on the house of the Others fixed. 1.1.0b Keeping pace with AGOT's 0.5.2 hotfix: an invasion war counts its goal as held once the dead occupy six tenths of it; the named dragons look the way AGOT now paints them; no camp with a dragon in it crosses an intact Wall. 1.1.0a — One Host The dead stop fighting the dead and keeping allies among the living; the Trial of Seven's roll call; the spear card's portraits; twelve fixes from a full playthrough log. 1.1.0 — The Last Hour The melee against the Night King; being raised as an Other; White Walkers in Winter Is Coming; memories; dragons over the Wall; a host that grows with his conquest; a field kill no longer ends the Long Night. 1.0.16a — The Wanderer The Night King keeps his land and pays his men; Send the Dungeons to the Wall; a limit on resurrections. 1.0.16 — The Dead That Frighten You The Others' culture; the strength rule rebuilt on advantage, damage and toughness; the Last Hour becomes a duel; the War for the Dawn gated on the dead losing a war. 1.0.15 — The Repair Release Killing him wins the war; Azor Ahai Reborn to the right man; only a bane destroys him; the Beric track; the Night King's face. 1.0.15a "Missing Title Loc" fixed for every other submod's rulers. 1.0.14 The Lord's Blessing works for players; AGOT 5.0 and 5.1; the North falls in order. 1.0.13 AGOT 0.5.1 compatibility; the mod stops shipping AGOT's rules file. 1.0.12 Lightbringer consecration; the Night King's spear; travel danger; the Great Ranging reworked. 1.0.11a The three cards that mark the turn of the age know who you are; the priest who names you has a face. 1.0.4 to 1.0.11 The struggle, the ranging companies, the Wall's castles, Send Men and Grain, the aftermath, the Russian translation. docs.x: This is a fork, and it stands on three people's work: Freeholder , who wrote the original AGOT: The Long Night ; Tehaen , who brought it forward to 1.19 as The Long Night (Resurrected) ; and Wepo94 , whose The Long Night+ added the wights, the Wall's collapse and the aftermath; and on the AGOT team's total conversion underneath all of it. The Night King's face was built by a player of the mod. Nearly every fix since August 2026 started as a report in the Discord or the Workshop comments, and reporters are credited by name in every changelog. If the AGOT team ever ships their own Long Night, this mod will come down and point at it. If they would rather lift anything from here into the base mod, it is theirs, no strings. Dlonem also maintains Supernatural . Everything else is at dlonem.com .

docs.x: Privacy policy Privacy Policy — Caffeine Break Buddy Effective July 5, 2026 Updated September 3, 2026 Publisher Dlonem LLC Contact caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com copy The short version. Caffeine Break Buddy is a personal caffeine-reset and habit-tracking app for Android (and for iOS, if released there later). Everything you log — your reset, intake calendar, daily check-ins, energy & sleep ratings, symptoms, badges, and the Caffeine & Sleep estimates — is stored only on your device . We run no servers and cannot see your data. The one exception is advertising : the free version shows ads through Google AdMob, which uses limited device and advertising identifiers to serve them. The one-time premium purchase removes ads. The app is an educational wellness tool — not a medical, diagnostic, or treatment service . Jump to a section 1. Who this applies to 2. What the app stores, and where 3. Advertising (free version) — Google AdMob 4. Data we process — at a glance 5. Purchases 6. What we do not do 7. Not medical advice 8. Children 9. Your choices & rights 10. Data security & retention 11. Changes to this policy 12. Contact 1 Who this applies to This policy covers the Caffeine Break Buddy mobile application published by Dlonem LLC on Google Play (and the Apple App Store , if released there later). The app is intended for a general adult audience. It is not directed to children, and we do not knowingly collect data from anyone under 13 (or the minimum age required by your region and the platform). 2 What the app stores, and where Caffeine Break Buddy is a local-first app. The information you enter is stored on your device only . Dlonem LLC operates no servers, no database, and no cloud storage of its own, and therefore has no access to this information and does not transmit it to us. What you can enter. Your onboarding profile (typical caffeine intake and delivery methods, timing, goal, and optional metabolism factors such as age range, sensitivity, smoking status, combined-pill / pregnancy status, and whether you take certain medications), your intake calendar, daily check-ins (energy, mood, headache, focus, sleep quality, cravings), milestone badges, and your bedtime/wake settings. This is used only to power the app's estimates and coaching on your device. No account, no cloud. The app has no sign-in and no server. Your data stays in this app's local storage on your device — we never receive, read, or store it, and it is not synced to any cloud by us. Optional manual backup. You can export a copy of your own data from within the app (Settings → Back up my data) and save it wherever you choose using your device's own share options, then import it later to restore. This is entirely manual and optional; the exported copy goes only where you send it. (On Android, the system's own Auto Backup may separately back up app data to your personal Google Drive under Google's terms — a platform feature we do not control or receive.) Deleting your data. You can reset your current break or erase everything from within the app (Settings → Reset this break / Start over). Uninstalling the app removes locally stored data from your device. 3 Advertising (free version) — Google AdMob The free version displays ads via Google AdMob (the Google Mobile Ads SDK). To serve and measure ads, AdMob may collect and process data such as your device's advertising identifier , IP address, general device information, and ad interactions, for advertising, analytics, and fraud-prevention purposes. Google handles this data under its own privacy policy. It is encrypted in transit and is kept separate from the personal reset data in Section 2 — AdMob does not receive your check-ins, symptoms, calendar, or profile answers. Google's handling of this data: policies.google.com/privacy and how Google uses information from partner apps . Android: you can reset or delete your advertising ID in Settings → Privacy → Ads. iOS — App Tracking Transparency (ATT): on Apple devices the app will ask for your permission before any tracking that uses your device's advertising identifier (IDFA). If you decline, ads may still be shown but will be non-personalized. You can change this any time in iOS Settings → Privacy & Security → Tracking. Region consent (EU/UK and similar): where required, you will be asked for ad-consent choices through Google's consent mechanism before personalized ads are shown. Removing ads: the one-time premium purchase removes all ads, after which the ad SDK no longer serves ads in the app. 4 Data we process — at a glance This table mirrors the answers you should give in Google Play's Data safety form and Apple's App Privacy questionnaire. Data Where it lives Purpose Linked to you / used to track? Reset, intake calendar, check-ins, energy/sleep ratings, symptoms, badges, profile & metabolism inputs On your device only (plus any manual backup copy you export yourself) App functionality you asked for No — never sent to us; not used for tracking Advertising ID, IP, device info, ad interactions Processed by Google AdMob Advertising, measurement, fraud prevention Used for ads by Google; on iOS only with your ATT permission Purchase record (that you bought premium) Google Play / Apple, on-device receipt Unlock premium; restore purchases Handled by the store; no card details reach us Note on health-related inputs: some optional profile answers (e.g. sensitivity, combined-pill / pregnancy status, medications) may be considered health-related. They are used only on your device to personalize your estimates, are never transmitted to us, and are never shared with the ad SDK. 5 Purchases The optional one-time premium purchase is processed by the platform's billing system — Google Play Billing on Android and Apple In-App Purchase (StoreKit) on iOS. We do not receive or store your payment-card details; the store handles the transaction under its own terms. A Restore Purchases option lets you re-unlock premium on a new device using the same store account. 6 What we do not do To be explicit: Dlonem LLC does not sell, rent, or trade your personal information; does not build advertising or marketing profiles from your reset data, check-ins, symptoms, or health-related answers; does not require an account, email, or sign-up to use the app; and operates no server or database that receives your tracking data. The only information that leaves your device is the limited advertising data handled by Google (Section 3) and, only if you choose it, an optional backup to your own personal cloud account. 7 Not medical advice Caffeine Break Buddy is an educational wellness and habit-tracking tool . Its recovery timelines, half-life and sleep-cutoff estimates, and coaching are informational only and are not medical advice, and do not diagnose, treat, cure, or prevent any condition . Estimates are approximations, not guarantees. Consult a qualified professional for medical advice, especially if you have a heart condition, are pregnant, or take medications. 8 Children The app is not directed to children and we collect no personal information from anyone — including children — because the app collects no data and transmits nothing to us. There is therefore nothing on our end for us to access or delete. Any data a user enters lives only on their own device and can be erased at any time within the app (Settings → Start over) or by uninstalling. 9 Your choices & rights Because your personal reset data stays on your device, you control it directly — view, edit, or erase it in the app at any time. For rights relating to ad data processed by Google (such as access or deletion requests under the GDPR, UK GDPR, or CCPA/CPRA), see Google's privacy policy linked in Section 3; you can also exercise ad choices via your device’s ad/tracking settings, or contact us with any privacy question at caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com . We will respond within a reasonable time. 10 Data security & retention Because your tracking data never leaves your device (except to a manual backup you choose to export yourself), it is protected by your device’s own operating-system security and any passcode or biometric lock you use. We retain none of it, because we never receive it — it lives only on your device for as long as you keep the app installed and is removed when you erase it in-app or uninstall. Advertising data processed by Google is retained by Google under its own policies. There is no server-side copy for us to lose, breach, or be compelled to disclose. 11 Changes to this policy We may update this policy as the app evolves or as store requirements change. Material changes will be reflected by updating the “Last updated” date above and, where appropriate, an in-app notice. Continued use of the app after an update means you accept the revised policy. 12 Contact Questions, requests, or concerns about this policy or your data: caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com . We will respond within a reasonable time. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com — that is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. © 2026 Dlonem LLC · Caffeine Break Buddy v1.0.0 · Questions? caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com

docs.x: The fine print Privacy policy Short, because there isn't much to disclose. Your data stays on your device. Per-app policies Pick your app Each app has its own dedicated policy. T THC Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: thcbreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy C Caffeine Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: caffeinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy N Nicotine Break Buddy Support & privacy contact: nicotinebreakbuddy@dlonem.com Read the policy D Tiny Dragon Hoard Support & privacy contact: tinydragonhoard@dlonem.com Read the policy The studio-wide version Effective date: July 14, 2026 · Last updated: August 16, 2026 Dlonem LLC ("Dlonem," "we," "us," "our") builds the mobile applications Tiny Dragon Hoard and the Break Buddy apps (together, the "Apps"). This policy explains what information the Apps handle and how. We built our Apps to be privacy-friendly; most of them run entirely on your device. Each app has its own support and privacy address, listed on that app’s policy page above. Use it for anything specific to that app. For company-level questions, contact@dlonem.com reaches us too. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com . That is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. Information you enter stays on your device The Break Buddy apps store what you enter (your tracking history, notes, and reminders) locally on your device. We do not collect it, send it to our servers, or have access to it. Deleting the app removes this data from your device. No accounts required You can use the Apps without creating an account or giving us your name, email, or other personal details. Advertising in the apps Some Apps display ads through Google AdMob. To serve ads, Google and its partners may collect and use certain device and usage information, including advertising identifiers, under Google's own policies. You can read more at policies.google.com/technologies/ads and manage ad personalization in your device settings. Apps that do not show ads do not collect this information. Cookies and similar technologies on this website This website (dlonem.com) sets no cookies of its own . It has no login, no shopping basket, and no first-party tracking. Where advertising is served on this site, however, advertising cookies set by third parties do apply, and the section below explains them. Advertising on this website Third-party vendors, including Google, use cookies to serve ads based on a user's prior visits to this website or other websites. Google's use of advertising cookies enables it and its partners to serve ads to you based on your visit to this site and/or other sites on the internet. You can opt out of personalised advertising at any time: Turn off personalised ads from Google in Google Ads Settings (also reachable at My Ad Center ). Opt out of personalised advertising from many other vendors at aboutads.info/choices or, in Europe, youronlinechoices.eu . Block or delete cookies in your browser settings. Doing so does not stop you seeing ads; it means the ones you see are less relevant. Third-party vendors other than Google may also serve ads on this site. Where they do, you can visit their own websites to opt out of their use of cookies for personalised advertising. Google's own explanation of how it uses data from sites that use its services is at policies.google.com/technologies/partner-sites . Where the law requires it (including under the GDPR in the EU and UK), you will be asked for consent before any personalised advertising cookies are set, and you can change or withdraw that choice at any time. Purchases In-app purchases are processed by Google Play Billing. We never see or store your payment details; Google handles the transaction. See Google's Privacy Policy for how that information is handled. Analytics Neither our Apps nor this website use third-party analytics tracking. We do not run Google Analytics or any equivalent, and we do not build advertising or marketing profiles from anyone's visit. (If this changes in the future, we will update this policy to disclose it.) Information sharing We do not sell your information. We do not share personal information with third parties except as needed to provide the services described above (for example, Google AdMob and Google Play Billing). Children's privacy Our Apps are not directed at children under 13, and we do not knowingly collect personal information from children. Security Because your tracking data stays on your device, its security is tied to your device's own protections. We encourage you to use a device passcode and keep your software up to date. Changes to this policy We may update this policy from time to time. Material changes will be posted on this page with a new effective date. Contact For questions about this policy, email contact@dlonem.com .

It is a lighthearted game for a general audience ; it is not specifically directed at children (see Section 8). 2 What the game stores, and where Tiny Dragon Hoard is a local-first game. The information the game creates is stored on your device only . Dlonem LLC operates no servers, no database, and no cloud storage of its own, and therefore has no access to your game data and does not transmit it to us. Your progress. Gold, gems, Dragon Stones, dragons and their perks, cosmetics, estates, milestones, daily streaks, high scores, and settings are saved locally so you can pick up where you left off. Purchase entitlements. The fact that you bought something (for example, “owns Clear Skies”) is stored locally so your unlocks persist and can be restored. No account of ours, and no cloud save. The game has no login of its own, and your progress is never uploaded anywhere by us. (Android’s system-level auto-backup may include app data in your own Google account backup, under Google’s terms — we never receive or read it.) Optional Google Play Games sign-in. If you choose to sign in to Google Play Games (it is optional, and the game works fully without it), the game submits your flight distances and Royal Bounty scores to Google’s leaderboards and reports achievement unlocks . We request family-appropriate ad content from AdMob to match the game’s cartoon tone. Where Google treats a player as a child under applicable rules, Google applies its own children’s-privacy protections, including non-personalized ad serving. Google’s handling of this data: policies.google.com/privacy and how Google uses information from partner apps . Region consent (EU/UK and similar): where required, you are asked for ad-consent choices through Google’s consent mechanism before any personalized ads are shown. Data Where it lives Purpose Linked to you / used to track? We will respond within a reasonable time. 8 Children’s privacy Tiny Dragon Hoard is a general-audience game and is not specifically directed at children. We take children’s privacy seriously and act in good faith under laws such as the U.S. Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA) and comparable rules: The game requires no account, name, email, or personal information to play — from anyone, child or adult. We do not knowingly collect personal information from children. Ads are served by Google AdMob; where Google treats a player as a child under applicable rules, Google applies its own children’s-privacy protections, including non-personalized ad serving. We do not create advertising or marketing profiles from any player’s activity. Purchases are real money and use the platform’s standard billing; we encourage parents to use device/store parental controls and purchase authentication (Google Play → Settings → “Require authentication for purchases”). A parent or guardian can remove any locally stored data at any time via the game (Settings → Reset Save Data) or by uninstalling, and can control spending with the device/store parental controls noted above. 9 Data security & retention Because your game data never leaves your device (except through your own device backups, if you use them), it is protected by your device’s own operating-system security and any passcode or biometric lock you use. We retain none of it, because we never receive it . The game makes no network connections of its own beyond the ad and billing services described above. 10 Changes to this policy If the game’s data practices ever change (for example, a future update adds a new service), we will update this policy and revise the dates above before the change takes effect. Material changes will be noted in the store listing or update notes. 11 Contact Dlonem LLC — tinydragonhoard@dlonem.com . Questions or concerns about this policy or your data? Email us any time and a human will get back to you. docs.t: How to Quit Nicotine: Cigarettes, Vapes and Pouches
docs.x: Quitting nicotine Quitting nicotine A plan for cigarettes, vapes and pouches: pick the day, choose your support, and get through the weeks that decide it. Start here What this guide covers From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The Nicotine Break Buddy page covers what nicotine does to your brain, the withdrawal timeline, and what the big trials say about quitting in general. This guide is the plan: choosing a day, choosing your support, what is different about vapes and pouches, and the things that catch people out in the first weeks. Quitting is much more likely to work with real support. Talk to a pharmacist or doctor about medication before your quit day. Step one Pick a quit day Smokefree.gov, run by the US National Cancer Institute, says to pick a day in the next two weeks: close enough that you do not lose your nerve, far enough away to get ready. The Institute's older quit booklet sums up the preparation in five steps, which work just as well for vapes and pouches as for cigarettes: Set a quit date. Tell family, friends and coworkers that you plan to quit. Anticipate the challenges you will face, and plan for them. Remove every product from your home, car, bag and desk: packs, pods, disposables, pouch tins, lighters. Talk to your doctor or pharmacist about help to quit. Step two Choose your medication before the day Nicotine replacement works better when you use it well, and the research is specific about what well means: Use two forms together. A patch for the steady background dose plus a fast-acting form (gum, lozenge, spray or inhaler) for cravings. Across 16 trials and more than 12,000 people, combining them raised long-term quit rates by about a quarter over using one form alone. The evidence is rated high certainty. Consider starting before quit day. Wearing the patch for a while before you stop, known as preloading, raised quit rates by about a quarter across nine trials. That evidence is moderate certainty. Ask a pharmacist how to do it. A bigger patch is not better. In the same review, a 42 or 44 mg patch did no better than the standard 21 or 22 mg one. Prescription options. Varenicline has some of the strongest evidence of any quit medication, and your doctor can say whether it suits you. Cytisine, a plant-derived medicine that works in a similar way, helped more people quit than placebo in the latest Cochrane review, and in the two trials comparing it with varenicline there was no clear difference, though that comparison is low certainty. It is prescription-only in the UK and sold over the counter in Canada and Poland. As of September 2026 it is not approved in the US: in June 2026 the FDA declined to approve it for now, citing manufacturing and labeling issues and not safety or effectiveness, and the company plans to reapply. One thing that is not a quit aid: nicotine pouches. The FDA has authorized some pouch products to be sold, which is not the same as approval, and none are approved to help people quit. Step three Line up a person, or a phone Call a quitline. In the US, 1-800-QUIT-NOW (or 1-855-DÉJELO-YA in Spanish) transfers you to your state's quitline, which is free and confidential. Coaches can help you get medication through your insurance or local programs. Among people who had already called a quitline, extra phone counselling raised the chance of quitting from about 7% to 10%. Or sign up for texts. Automated text programs raise quit rates compared with minimal support, according to a Cochrane review that rates the evidence as moderate certainty. Three free ones: SmokefreeTXT: text QUIT to 47848. It runs for six to eight weeks. CDC's texting portal: text QUITNOW to 333888. EX Program by Truth Initiative, which now includes the This is Quitting vaping program: text EXPROGRAM to 88709. It is open to anyone 13 or older. Message and data rates may apply. Not just cigarettes Vapes and pouches Quitting a vape or pouch habit starts with working out how much nicotine you actually take, and that is harder than counting cigarettes. Vapes. In US sales data, the average nicotine concentration of disposable vapes rose to 48.5 mg/mL by mid-2024, and the average amount of liquid in each device grew from 1.6 mL to 11.7 mL. One disposable can hold far more nicotine than it looks like. The UK caps e-liquid at 20 mg/mL and tanks at 2 mL. Nicotine salts, used in most disposables, let people take high levels without the harshness that would otherwise stop them. Pouches. US products tested by the CDC ranged from about 1.3 to 6.1 mg of nicotine per pouch. European products tested in another study reached 47.5 mg per pouch. Check the tin, and count pouches per day, not tins per week. What helps people quit vaping. The evidence is newer but growing: In a 2025 trial of 16 to 25-year-olds who vaped but did not smoke, 51% of those given varenicline were abstinent in weeks 9 to 12, against 14% on placebo; both groups also got counselling. By weeks 9 to 24 it was 28% against 7%. In trials of the This is Quitting text program, 24% of young adults quit, against 19% of those without it, and among teens 38% against 28%. A 2025 Cochrane review concluded that varenicline may help people stop vaping and text-message programs may help young people. For combination nicotine replacement and cytisine, the evidence on vaping is still inconclusive. The first weeks Three things that catch people out Alcohol. Smokefree.gov puts it plainly: for many people alcohol is a trigger that makes them want to smoke, and it makes you more likely to act without thinking it through. A 2023 review found drinking linked to lower quit success in 20 of 27 studies. Stay away from it for the first few weeks if you can. Coffee, if you smoked. Tobacco smoke speeds up the enzyme that clears caffeine; smokers clear it about 56% faster. When you stop smoking, that effect fades within days: in one study, caffeine clearance fell by about a third, and in another, four days off cigarettes raised the amount of caffeine in the blood over a day by 46%. Levels can stay higher for months. The result is that your usual coffee hits harder, and the jitters and poor sleep that follow are easy to mistake for nicotine withdrawal. New Zealand's medicines regulator suggests halving your caffeine when you quit. This comes from the smoke, not the nicotine. It happens when you stop smoking even if you use nicotine replacement, and it does not apply if what you are quitting is a vape or pouches. The caffeine guide shows how to count and cut back. Your other medicines, if you smoked. The same enzyme handles several prescription drugs. Doses of clozapine, olanzapine, theophylline and warfarin may need to come down when a smoker quits. If you take any of these, tell your prescriber before your quit day, not after. The target Aim for 28 days The NHS sets the first goal at 28 days without smoking, because people who reach it are five times more likely to quit for good. It turns an open-ended promise into a date on the calendar, and most of the hardest stretch is behind you well before you get there. If it happens If you slip A slip is not the end of the attempt. Smokefree.gov says it directly: you have not failed and you are not back to square one, and most people need several tries before they stop for good. What you do in the next hour matters more than the slip itself: Get rid of the rest. Do not keep the pack, the disposable or the tin "to finish it." Go back to the plan straight away, the same day. Not on Monday. Work out what set it off: the place, the time, the person, the drink. Check your medication. Are you using the patch every day and the fast-acting form when cravings hit, as directed? Under-dosing is a common reason cravings win. The app Keep count Nicotine Break Buddy is the tracker I built for this. It works for cigarettes, vapes, pouches and dip, and has a 60-second breathing timer for riding out a craving, quick daily check-ins, money saved counting up, and a Comeback badge for logging a slip instead of hiding it. It needs no account, and nothing you enter leaves your phone. It is free on Android: get it here . Taking a break from something else? There is a guide to cutting back on caffeine and one to cannabis tolerance breaks . References Sources Smokefree.gov (National Cancer Institute). Build your quit plan. Link National Cancer Institute. Clearing the Air: Quit Smoking Today (START steps). Link Theodoulou A et al. Different doses, durations and modes of delivery of nicotine replacement therapy for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews , 2023. Link Livingstone-Banks J et al. Nicotine receptor partial agonists for smoking cessation. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews , 2023. Link NCSCT. Cytisine briefing, 2026. Link Achieve Life Sciences. Complete Response Letter from FDA for cytisinicline NDA, June 2026. Link CDC. Nicotine pouches. Link US FDA. FDA authorizes marketing of 20 ZYN nicotine pouch products

docs.t: Support — help with Dlonem apps and CK3 mods
docs.x: Support Get help If you found a bug, hit a snag, or have a feature idea, I’d like to hear about it. Everything here reaches one person (me), so be as specific as you like. Email contact@dlonem.com Home › Support Where to write Anything sent to contact@dlonem.com reaches me, so if you are unsure, use that. If you already know which app you are writing about, its own address gets there a step faster. Each one is listed on that app’s privacy policy page , alongside the policy itself. Replies come from officialdlonem@gmail.com . That is us, not spam; the @dlonem.com addresses receive mail but cannot send it. For the Crusader Kings III mods, Discord is faster than email. Bug reports land in front of me and the rest of the community at the same time, and someone has usually hit your problem already: The Long Night Discord , for The Long Night & Azor Ahai Supernatural Discord , for the Supernatural mod Getting a faster answer I aim to respond within a few business days. To help me help you faster, include: The app or mod name , for example Tiny Dragon Hoard or The Long Night Your device model and Android/iOS version, or for a mod, your CK3 and AGOT versions What you expected to happen, and what happened instead For a mod, your load order and any other mods you are running (most mod problems turn out to be two mods disagreeing) A screenshot is worth several paragraphs. If an app crashed, telling me what you tapped immediately before it happened is usually the single most useful detail. Questions that come up a lot Where is my tracking data stored? On your device. The Break Buddy apps keep what you enter (history, notes and reminders) locally. I do not collect it, and I cannot read it. That is also why I cannot recover it for you if a phone is lost, which is what the in-app backup export is for. Do I need an account? No. None of the apps need an account. Tiny Dragon Hoard offers an optional Google Play Games sign-in for leaderboards and achievements; everything else works without signing in to anything. Is there a subscription? No. The apps are free, and where there is a paid unlock it is a one-time purchase. I am not going to charge you monthly for a habit tracker. I bought the unlock and changed phones. How do I get it back? Your unlock is tied to the store account you bought it with, so signing in to the same Google Play or App Store account restores it. Note that restoring one of the app’s own backup files will not carry the unlock across. Entitlement always comes from the store, never from an imported file, and the apps are written to keep it that way. When is the iOS version out? THC Break Buddy is on the App Store now. Caffeine Break Buddy, Nicotine Break Buddy and Tiny Dragon Hoard are Android-only for the moment. Each app page shows its current status on both stores. That is the page I keep up to date, so it will always be ahead of anything I could write here. A mod is not working. What should I check first? Load order and conflicting mods, in that order. Both mod pages carry their own FAQ covering load order, compatibility with other mods, and whether you need to start a new save; see The Long Night & Azor Ahai or Supernatural . If you are running both of my mods together, you also need the compatibility patch, which is explained on the mods page . Can I install the mods without Steam? Yes. Both mods have a manual download route with step-by-step instructions, linked from the mods page . Something in an app looks wrong or overlaps If text is colliding or a ring looks squashed, check your phone’s system font-size setting first. A very large display font can push layouts past what they were designed for. Tell me your font-size setting when you report it and it saves us both a round trip. Feature ideas Feature ideas are welcome, and a fair number of the things in these apps started as somebody’s email. I cannot promise a timeline, and I will tell you if something does not fit the app rather than leaving you waiting on it.

docs.t: The Game Center — a Discord server since 2016
docs.x: Est. May 2016 The Game Center The first server I ever made, and the one that turned into a community by accident. It is still running. How it started The real reason I made it In May 2016 my friend group was still calling each other on Skype, which meant somebody had to start the call and everybody had to be there for it. I found Discord before most people had heard of it, showed everyone, and they took to it immediately. I will be honest about the next part, because it is the real reason. I made the server because I wanted to be the one who owned it. I could see where this was going and I wanted to get there first. It is not a noble founding story, but it is a true one. It began as a room for fewer than fifty people to play Dota in, with a plain controller icon and no ambitions. Within a year there were two hundred and fifty of us. People brought friends, those friends brought friends, and at some point it stopped being a group chat. The first website Eight characters you cannot copy Here is a problem that sounds trivial and was not. You cannot copy and paste out of a video game. If you met someone in a match and wanted to invite them, you had to read eight random characters aloud and hope they typed them correctly. So I built a website. One page, one button. Go to the address, click join, you are in the room. That was the whole product, and it worked. I was not a web developer and it showed. That site is long gone, but the idea was right. This page is the same idea, built with more care, nine years later. The point of it Especially the quiet ones In 2017 I wrote myself a set of messages to send to people who had joined and then never said anything. It was not a moderation thing; I did not like the idea of somebody sitting in a server for months feeling like they were not part of it. One was written specifically for people who do not talk because they are shy, or because walking into a room where everyone already knows each other is hard. The gist of it: the regulars are good people, we post nonsense daily, and not knowing anyone yet should not be the thing that stops you. That is still the idea. I wanted the bar where everybody knows your name, with considerably more Dota. The hard part Keeping a room comfortable Wanting a place where quiet people feel welcome sounds simple until you have to enforce it. It started with slurs, which was easy; nobody serious argued the point. Then it was people telling each other to go kill themselves, and that is where I stopped treating any of it as banter. I brought in bots that caught those phrases, deleted the message, and sometimes removed the person with it. Then came the pushback: too much censorship. I never agreed and I still do not. What got removed was a short list of things whose only purpose is to make somebody feel small. Everything else was fair game. We opened an uncensored channel where anyone could say whatever they liked, and almost nobody used it, which told me the objection was never about wanting to say those things. A server where the loudest people set the rules is a server the quiet ones leave, without saying anything. What we did Game nights and Christmas mugs We ran Dota 2 in-house nights: twelve against twelve, any rank welcome, a voice channel per team, with fallbacks for when not enough people turned up. In hindsight they were held together with tape: I was organising instead of playing and the teams were assembled largely on vibes. They were also some of the best nights the server ever had. For four Decembers I ran holiday giveaways: mugs, shirts, stickers, and a pile of games bought out of my own pocket. No sponsor and no angle. People had been good to each other all year and it seemed like the right way to say so. I stopped after 2021, which felt like the right place to stop. The trade What it cost The server worked. That is also what broke it for the people who were there first. The original group slowly stopped showing up: too many people, too many strangers, too much noise. One of my oldest friends has never liked being in a room with people he does not know, and by then that is exactly what this was. I spent years pushing to get more people in, which was the same act as pushing my friends out. I did not see it that way at the time. So I made them a smaller, private one instead, and that is the one they still use. Which brings me back to owning things. I like making things I control (servers, apps, mods, this website). I hardly ever use the power, but I like having it, because I do not entirely trust other people with it. That is why it took me so long to hand anyone else the keys, and why some of the drama that eventually split the server was other people wanting exactly the same thing. Nine years on A tenth of a percent Someone who joined here as a teenager and left for college once told me this was the server he grew up in. You cannot design that. You can only leave the door open long enough for it to happen to somebody. I figure I own about a tenth of a percent of a lot of people's brains. Somebody mentions Discord servers, and somewhere out there a person goes: oh, The Game Center — yeah, I used to be in that. It happened almost entirely because I would not stop asking people to join. The door is still open If that invite ever stops working, this one goes to the same place. The other rooms There are three more The Game Center is the oldest of four Discord servers I run, and the rest are on the Community page . Dlonem's Den goes with the YouTube channel ; the other two are for my Crusader Kings III mods, The Long Night & Azor Ahai and Supernatural .

docs.t: How to Take a Tolerance Break That Sticks
docs.x: Cannabis tolerance break Taking a tolerance break How long to go, how to get ready, how to get through the nights, and how to come back without undoing it. Start here What this guide covers From Dlonem · Updated 27 September 2026 · General information, not medical advice The THC Break Buddy page explains why tolerance happens and what each stretch of a break feels like, day by day. This guide covers everything around a tolerance break, or T-break as most people call it: choosing a length, getting ready, getting through the nights, and what to do on the last day so you are not back here in two months. If you use cannabis for a diagnosed condition, plan any break with the clinician who knows about it. Choosing a length How long it needs to be Two brain-imaging studies have tracked what happens to cannabinoid (CB1) receptors when daily users stop. In the first, heavy users had about 20% fewer receptors than non-users in parts of the brain, and after roughly four weeks of monitored abstinence the gap was gone. The second scanned 11 cannabis-dependent men: their receptors were about 15% lower at the start, the difference was no longer significant after just two days, and it was still gone at day 28. It was a small study of men only, so read it as "recovery starts quickly," not "two days is enough." What those scans measure is receptors. How strongly you feel the effect afterwards has not been measured the same way, so the length you choose is partly a judgment call. The withdrawal timeline is the other half of it. In the study that mapped it, symptoms usually began on days one to three, peaked between days two and six, and mostly lasted four to fourteen days. Length What you get 2 to 4 days Receptor recovery has started, but you stop in the middle of the worst stretch. All of the discomfort, little of the payoff. About 2 weeks For most people the withdrawal is over and the break has stopped being hard. About 4 weeks The point at which both imaging studies found receptor levels no different from non-users. Longer than a month Worth it if the goal is to change the pattern and not only the tolerance. See the section on coming back . The week before Getting ready Count forward from your start day. Days two to six are the hard ones, so look at what falls on them. A start day that puts day four on a work deadline or a family visit is a start day worth moving. Decide what happens to what is left. Finish it before day one, give it away, or put it somewhere that takes real effort to reach. More breaks end because something was within arm's reach at 11pm than because of a craving that could not be managed. If you mix with tobacco, decide about that now. Spliffs and blunts mean a cannabis break is also a nicotine break unless you keep smoking tobacco on its own. In a small study, stopping both at once was harder than stopping either alone for the first few days, though the difference was short-lived and varied from person to person. In another, cigarette use went up by about 14 a week during a two-week cannabis break, and poor sleep predicted who smoked more. Either plan can work. Know which one you are on before day one, and if you are stopping both, the nicotine guide covers that side. Set up sleep before you need it. Pick a wake-up time you will keep every day of the break, and set a caffeine cutoff. In a sleep-lab study, 400 mg of caffeine taken six hours before bed still cut total sleep by more than an hour. The caffeine guide has a way to count what you actually drink. Know what the first week will feel like, and why. Anxiety, irritability, low mood and trouble sleeping are all on the formal list of cannabis withdrawal symptoms. If those are the reasons you use, the first week can feel like proof that you need it. It is withdrawal, and it passes on the schedule above. Not everyone's week is the same Why some breaks are harder A 2020 review of 47 studies and more than 23,000 people found cannabis withdrawal syndrome in about 47% of regular users. It was more common with daily use and with tobacco use alongside cannabis. A separate review puts it simply: the heavier and longer the use before stopping, the stronger the withdrawal. Potency matters in a related way. Frequent use of high-potency cannabis has been linked to more severe dependence, while low-potency use was not associated with dependence in the same study. Concentrate users have shown greater physiological dependence even after accounting for other factors. Neither study measured withdrawal directly, so treat it as a reason to plan for a rougher first week, not as a prediction. Women also tend to report stronger withdrawal, including physical symptoms such as nausea and stomach pain. If you use daily, use concentrates or mix with tobacco, give yourself the longer runway: a start day with a quiet week after it, and the sleep setup below in place from the first night. Sleep Getting through the nights Sleep is where most breaks are won or lost. In sleep-lab studies, heavy users slept less and spent less time in deep sleep during their first nights off. In one that recorded people across nearly two weeks of abstinence, total sleep and sleep efficiency went down while time spent awake in the night went up. Strange, vivid dreams are one of the most common complaints, and in one outpatient study sleep trouble and odd dreams were still being reported up to seven weeks in. The research does not agree on the details of what changes, but it agrees that sleep gets worse before it gets better. The techniques that work for insomnia generally work here too: Get up at the same time every day, including after a bad night. It is the single anchor the rest depends on. Go to bed when you are sleepy, not at a set time because you think you should. If you are still awake after 15 to 20 minutes, get up. Do something calm in low light and go back when you feel sleepy. Lying there trying teaches your brain that bed is where you lie awake. Keep the bed for sleep. No scrolling, no shows in bed while this is going on. Skip long naps. They take the edge off the sleep pressure you need at night. Watch the swap. Alcohol helps you fall asleep, then breaks up sleep in the second half of the night and delays dreaming sleep. In one study, people on a two-week cannabis break drank about eight more standard drinks a week. Another found the increase only in people with a past alcohol problem. If that describes you, it is the part of the break to plan for most carefully. If sleep has not started improving after a few weeks, or you are thinking about sleep medication, that is a conversation for a pharmacist or doctor. After When the break ends How a break ends matters as much as how long it lasts. A 2023 study followed 170 young adults for six months. Those who took breaks specifically to lower their tolerance were using more hazardously six months later, while those who took longer breaks for other reasons were using less. It was an observational study, so it cannot show the break caused anything. It does match the rest of the research, which consistently ties tolerance to how often you use: regular users feel less from the same amount, and more frequent use goes with a weaker high. Return to the old frequency and you are rebuilding the old tolerance. So decide the pattern before the last day, and write it down: How many days a week, and which ones. This is the number that does the most to keep tolerance down. How much, to start. Much less than you used to. Your tolerance is lower than your habits remember. What you use. Lower-potency products were not associated with dependence in the research above; high-potency ones were. One safety point. Tolerance is partial and it differs by effect. In a study of 122 users, the effect of cannabis on thinking and reaction tests was similar whether people used rarely or heavily. Feeling less high is not the same as being less impaired, and it is not a reason to drive. When it is not about tolerance Signs it is more than a tolerance problem Tolerance and withdrawal are two of the eleven criteria for cannabis use disorder. The others include using more or for longer than intended, repeated attempts to cut down that do not stick, giving up things you care about, and carrying on despite problems it is causing. A diagnosis is a clinician's call and turns on whether use is causing real problems or distress. If you have tried a break several times and never got past the first week, that is worth taking to one. Cannabinoid hyperemesis syndrome is worth knowing by name. It shows up in long-term regular users as repeated bouts of severe nausea and vomiting, often with stomach pain. A strong urge to take hot showers or baths, which bring relief, is a telltale sign: in a systematic review, 92% of cases had it.
